It combines a centralized knowledge base, interactive training, task management, forms and checklists, audits, a location launcher for opening new stores, team communication, and reporting so franchisors can standardize and enforce standard operating procedures across every location. The platform is built around frontline franchisee adoption and serves 150+ franchise brands across food and beverage, fitness, wellness, home services, and other multi-unit, regulated sectors. Backed by Accel; profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment (2026-07-18).

companies.name: Valence (FKA Shift)
companies.description: Valence (formerly Shift) is an enterprise AI coaching platform backed by Insight Partners. Its flagship product, Nadia, is an AI leadership coach that helps managers and their teams adopt AI, build skills, and improve teamwork, alongside team tools Align, Habit, Perspective, Reflect 360, and Connect. The platform is enterprise SaaS with SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, certified SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001, and publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Federal Student Aid
companies.description: The Federal Student Aid (FSA) office of the U.S. Department of Education provides grants, loans, and work-study funds to eligible students enrolled in college or career school. FSA operates StudentAid.gov as the consumer portal for managing federal student loans, completing the FAFSA, and exploring repayment options. FSA does not currently publish a public, open developer API program; aggregate higher education and aid data is redistributed through the Department of Education's open data programs such as the College Scorecard API.

companies.name: Platformable
companies.description: Platformable provides API governance, open ecosystem intelligence, and consultancy services. Their training resources, dashboards, and tools help organizations build comprehensive, automated, high quality API governance systems and participate in open digital ecosystems including open banking, digital health, and traceability.

companies.name: United States Botanic Garden
companies.description: The United States Botanic Garden (USBG) is a living museum in Washington, D.C. that showcases a diverse collection of plants from around the world. Established by the U.S. Congress in 1820, the Botanic Garden serves as a resource for education and inspiration, promoting an understanding and appreciation of plants and their importance to the environment and human well-being. The Garden maintains more than 9,500 accessions representing approximately 44,000 plants, managed through its Living Collections database (BG-BASE). The USBG is administered by the Architect of the Capitol and is located adjacent to the U.S. Capitol on the National Mall.

companies.name: Wonder Workshop
companies.description: Wonder Workshop (GitHub org "playi", originally Play-i) is an educational technology company that makes the Dash, Dot, and Cue programmable robots and the Make Wonder K-8 coding and robotics learning platform, used by more than 40,000 schools across 65 countries. Its developer surface is a set of official SDKs that give granular realtime control of the physical robots' sensors and actuators over Bluetooth Low Energy: WonderPy (Python, on PyPI), @wonderworkshop/wwjs (JavaScript, on npm), and an iOS/Android robot framework shipped in the playground sample-app repository. There is no HTTP/cloud REST API, OAuth, or webhook surface; integration happens locally over BLE. Backed by GV.

companies.name: Lamina Labs
companies.description: Lamina Labs is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building near-real-time video infrastructure for large language models. Its flagship product, Simi, turns prompts, documents, and AI-generated answers into whiteboard-style teaching videos in seconds, handling script writing, illustration, animation, and narration automatically, for durations from one minute to an hour and in over 80 languages. The company targets training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and educational use cases, with the stated goal of making video the default interface for AI communication. Lamina exposes Simi to agents through a public remote MCP server at https://api.laminalabs.ai/mcp, secured by an OAuth 2.1-style authorization server with PKCE, dynamic client registration, and job-scoped access tokens.

companies.name: Queen Mary University of London
companies.description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is a public research university in London, United Kingdom, and a member of the Russell Group, ranked #120 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-oriented rather than a formal developer program: Queen Mary Research Online (QMRO) is an open-access DSpace institutional repository that exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, and the university maintains a public GitHub organization (QMUL) for code released by its staff. QMUL does not publish a central, branded developer portal with signup-gated REST APIs; core student, timetable, and library platforms (QMplus/Moodle, MyQMUL, library discovery) sit behind institutional authentication.

companies.name: Tianjin University
companies.description: Tianjin University (TJU) is a national public research university in Tianjin, China, founded in 1895 as Peiyang University and recognized as the oldest modern university in China. It is ranked #269 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. TJU operates the usual institutional web properties (official site, library OPAC, faculty and international-cooperation portals) but does not publish a public developer portal or documented, openly accessible API. No public API documentation, base URLs, or sign-up flows could be verified at the time of cataloging; the entries below reflect only confirmed public web properties, not documented APIs.

companies.name: Wuhan University
companies.description: Wuhan University (WHU), founded in 1893 and located in Wuhan, Hubei, China, is one of China's oldest and most prestigious comprehensive research universities, ranked #194 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates under the Ministry of Education of China and is recognized for surveying and remote sensing, geoinformatics, and the sciences. WHU does not publish a centralized, publicly documented developer or API portal; its official web presence (en.whu.edu.cn) is informational only. Discoverable developer activity is concentrated in research-group GitHub organizations rather than institutional API products. No public, documented institutional API endpoints could be confirmed at the time of review.

companies.name: NutriSense
companies.description: NutriSense is a metabolic health and wellness company that pairs continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with 1:1 registered-dietitian coaching and a mobile app. Members receive glucose biosensors, real-time and historical glucose analytics, AI-assisted pattern insights, stress-management sessions, and video consults with credentialed, glucose-certified nutritionists to build sustainable nutrition, weight-loss, and metabolic-health habits. Nutrisense runs a consumer product with a member web and mobile app experience; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It does publish a machine-readable llms.txt at nutrisense.io/llms.txt.

companies.name: Udemy
companies.description: Udemy is a global online learning marketplace offering tens of thousands of on-demand video courses across business, technology, design, and personal development, alongside Udemy Business, an enterprise learning subscription for workforce skills development. Udemy exposes REST APIs including the Affiliate API for course discovery and the Instructor API for instructor resources, both using bearer token authentication over HTTPS with JSON-formatted responses.

companies.name: Guidde
companies.description: Guidde is an AI-powered digital adoption and knowledge-capture platform that turns any on-screen workflow into professional step-by-step video documentation and how-to guides. Its Magic Capture browser extension, desktop, and mobile apps record a process, then AI generates a structured script, an AI voiceover (200+ voices), and an editable walkthrough that teams can translate into 50+ languages and embed wherever work happens. Guidde targets onboarding, customer education, support deflection, and internal process documentation for enterprises, and integrates with tools like Slack, Zendesk, Confluence, Notion, Salesforce, SharePoint, and ServiceNow. Guidde is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Guidde does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: BrainCo
companies.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

companies.name: Wonderschool
companies.description: Wonderschool is a child care platform that connects families with licensed care and equips providers with software and services to start, operate, and grow their child care programs. It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

companies.name: Educative
companies.description: Educative is an online learning platform that provides high-quality, interactive courses for developers of all skill levels. With a focus on practical, hands-on learning, Educative offers courses on a wide range of topics, from programming languages like Python and JavaScript to data structures and algorithms. Each course is created by expert instructors and includes quizzes, coding challenges, and real-world projects to help learners apply their knowledge.

companies.name: Hiphen Plant
companies.description: Hiphen Plant provides advanced image analytics solutions for agricultural research. As plant scientists, they build tools that revolutionize how plants can be assessed, bringing the power of image analytics to agricultural research programs for decision-making on genetics, chemistry, and practices.

companies.name: Brisk Teaching
companies.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.

companies.name: Caliber Fitness
companies.description: Caliber Fitness, Inc. is a consumer strength-training and fitness-coaching company behind the Caliber: Strength Training app (iOS and Android). Caliber combines data-driven resistance-training and nutrition programming, a library of 600+ exercises, workout tracking, and one-on-one video coaching from certified personal trainers across free, Caliber Plus, and Premium Coaching tiers. Founded by Justin Fauci and Chris Muir, the company is backed by Trinity Ventures. Caliber operates as a consumer mobile app and coaching service; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. This profile tracks its public web, legal, and membership surface within the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Floreo
companies.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

companies.name: IKI AI
companies.description: IKI AI is an AI-native workspace for knowledge, research, strategy, and creative work, backed by 500 Global. It pairs an AI assistant that summarizes, highlights, and connects saved content with an AI editor that grounds writing in a user's personal knowledge base, plus shared Team Spaces and a browser extension for one-click webpage saving with notes. The product targets researchers, students, consultants, copywriters, coaches, lawyers, founders, and venture teams, and emphasizes privacy with a choice of top-tier LLMs. IKI AI is delivered as a consumer and team SaaS (web app at app.iki.ai and a Chrome extension) with subscription plans; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. This profile tracks its public identity, commercial, and security surface in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: MentorCloud
companies.description: MentorCloud is an AI-enabled, enterprise mentoring software platform that helps organizations optimize employee engagement, retention, and career development through structured mentoring programs. It serves HR and Learning & Development teams and enterprise leaders looking to scale human-led learning across engineering, management, higher education, hospitality, and non-profit contexts. The platform covers mentor/mentee matching, program management, sessions, circles, learning, and community, with use cases spanning new-hire onboarding, leadership development, career progression, and Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. MentorCloud is delivered as a hosted B2B SaaS product with managed, custom two-way integrations to enterprise CRM, HR, and single sign-on systems rather than a self-serve public developer API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)
companies.description: The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) is part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health and supports research into the causes, treatment, and prevention of arthritis and musculoskeletal and skin diseases. NIAMS publishes health information, research resources, and grant data via its website.

companies.name: GreatSchools
companies.description: GreatSchools provides school information, ratings, and quality data via its Developer Hub APIs, including the School Essentials API for school details and the School Quality API for GreatSchools rating bands.

companies.name: Newsela
companies.description: Newsela is a K-12 content and assessment platform that provides research-backed, engaging, differentiated reading content and AI-powered tools across ELA, social studies, STEM, and writing to support educators and drive student growth in grades 3-12. Newsela publishes no public developer API; it integrates with school systems as a certified 1EdTech (IMS Global) product supporting OneRoster 1.1 rostering, LTI v1.3 launch, and Data Privacy certification, and handles student data under FERPA, COPPA, and state student-privacy laws. Added to the API Evangelist network as a techstars portfolio company.

companies.name: Piper Inc.
companies.description: Piper (Piper Learning, Inc. / Piper LLC) is an educational-technology company that makes hands-on STEM learning kits — most notably the Piper Computer Kit, a buildable wooden computer that teaches circuitry and coding through Minecraft, and Piper Make, a browser-based platform for exploring electronics and Python. Its consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with an MCP endpoint plus Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect, letting AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and check out with explicit buyer approval. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its live public agent/discovery surface.

companies.name: Unmind
companies.description: Unmind is a workplace mental health platform that supports employees, develops leaders, and strengthens organisational performance through therapy, coaching, manager training, crisis care, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), wellbeing content, insights and assessments, and Nova, an AI wellbeing coach. Customers include Uber, MLB, Samsung, British Airways, Diageo, and the NHS. Unmind publishes no public developer API; api.unmind.com is a private Apollo GraphQL backend serving its own apps.

companies.name: Edison Scientific
companies.description: Edison Scientific is an AI research company building Kosmos, an autonomous "AI Scientist" for R&D teams in drug discovery and biopharma. Kosmos reads scientific literature, analyzes experimental data, generates and tests hypotheses, and executes research workflows autonomously, collaborating with scientists through tools like Slack and Teams. The model-agnostic platform spans the drug development lifecycle from target identification through clinical development and filing, learning from proprietary organizational and scientific data. Edison Labs publishes open science research including the PaperQA line of multimodal deep research agents. The company is backed by Spark Capital and maintains an enterprise Trust Center with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture. No public developer API is published at this time.

companies.name: Hallo
companies.description: Hallo is an AI-powered language assessment and language-learning company backed by Battery Ventures. Its enterprise platform delivers automated, AI-driven proficiency assessments across speaking, writing, listening, and reading in 80+ languages, with CEFR-aligned scoring, detailed feedback (fluency, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, coherence), real-time score reports and dashboards, and proctoring / anti-cheating for high-stakes hiring, placement testing, and employee development. Hallo integrates with major applicant-tracking systems (Greenhouse, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Lever, SuccessFactors, Recruitee, and others) and runs assessments across 160+ countries, with a stated SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and EU AI Act compliance posture. The company also operates a consumer language-learning app with AI tutors and native-speaker practice. Hallo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; its integration surface is delivered through prebuilt ATS connectors and enterprise onboarding rather than a self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: Kodable
companies.description: Kodable is a San Diego, California based educational technology company that makes self-guided coding, computer science, and digital literacy games for elementary school students in grades K-5. Its product line includes Kodable Basics (an introduction to programming concepts for pre-readers), Kodable Creator (game design and coding with AI-assisted tutoring), Kodable Typing (keyboarding practice), and Bug World (JavaScript and object-oriented programming). Kodable sells to elementary schools and districts as well as directly to parents, pairing the student games with a teacher dashboard, K-5 curriculum, lesson plans, and professional development. The company is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory and a member of the Student Data Privacy Consortium, and publishes a privacy center covering COPPA, its EULA, terms of service, and district Data Privacy Agreement review. Kodable was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Kodable publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts - it is a consumer and school facing application rather than an API provider.

companies.name: Inkling
companies.description: Inkling is a frontline employee training and enablement platform (now part of Echo360) that delivers mission-critical knowledge, learning pathways, and operational workflows to essential workers across retail, hospitality, healthcare, and manufacturing. Its products include the Habitat content authoring tool, mobile Knowledge & Training modules, InkForms operational checklists, certification pathways, reporting and analytics, and LMS/LXP integrations. Inkling publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through LMS/LXP connectors and professional services. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched with the provider's public identity, security posture, and site properties.

companies.name: Literati
companies.description: Literati is an Austin, Texas based children's book company founded by Jessica Ewing that operates three connected consumer and school businesses: personalized monthly Book Clubs for Kids that ship five curated books matched to a child's reading level and interests starting at $11.95 per month, Clubs for Classrooms for teachers, and a school book fair business (in-person and online) run through the OpenBook coordinator dashboard at openbook.literati.com and the year-round Literati Store, which returns a share of proceeds to participating schools. The company draws on 150+ publishers, combines expert curation with data science to personalize book selection, and reports more than one million books donated to Title I schools and underserved communities since 2019. Literati publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; its public technical surface is limited to consumer and school-facing web applications, iOS and Android apps, and an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-reporting contact.

companies.name: memrise
companies.description: Memrise is a language-learning app founded in 2010 and headquartered in London, UK, trusted by 80 million learners across iOS, Android, and web. It is built around real native-speaker video, goal-based specialised courses (exams, work, relationships, travel), a spaced-repetition memory-science engine created by co-founder and Princeton neuroscientist Greg Detre, and AI conversation practice. Memrise offers courses in 149+ languages and has been profitable since 2016. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. Memrise is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and machine-readable (llms.txt) surface.

companies.name: Sakana AI
companies.description: Sakana AI is a Tokyo-based AI R&D company founded by ex-Google researchers focused on collective intelligence, evolutionary optimization, and nature-inspired AI methods. The company's first commercial product is Sakana Fugu - a multi-agent orchestration system with an OpenAI-compatible API (currently in beta). Sakana also publishes Sakana Chat (consumer) and Sakana Marlin (beta).

companies.name: Aristotle
companies.description: Aristotle (heyaristotle.com) is an AI tutoring platform that delivers personalized, one-on-one, dialogue-based instruction across all subjects. Rather than lecturing or simply marking answers wrong, it uses a Socratic, voice-first approach to diagnose conceptual misconceptions and verifies each response turn-by-turn before delivering it to the student. Positioned as an affordable alternative to human tutors, its methodology is grounded in learning science (Bloom's two-sigma work, ICAP, LearnLM benchmarks). Backed by True Ventures. Sector: EdTech / AI education. No public developer API or SDK surface at this time.

companies.name: Blackboard
companies.description: Blackboard (now part of Anthology) provides Blackboard Learn LMS plus the Anthology product suite (Ally, Student). The Anthology Developer portal exposes REST APIs for Learn, Ally, and Student, with versions across the 3200, 3900, and 4000 series and ongoing backward compatibility.

companies.name: Coursebase
companies.description: Coursebase is an AI-powered corporate Learning Management System (LMS) used by over 1,000 organizations to create, deliver, and manage employee training across online, in-person, and blended formats. The platform offers a library of 1,000+ pre-built eLearning courses, AI-assisted content generation (auto-generated test questions and course summaries), analytics and reporting dashboards, single sign-on, multi-language support, and API-based integration with external HR systems for syncing user account information. Coursebase was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched in the API Evangelist network; the public surface is a marketing site with an enterprise "contact us" API integration offering rather than a self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI.

companies.name: Simpleclub
companies.description: Simpleclub is a German digital learning platform serving over two million students (grades 5-13), apprentices, and organizations across school, vocational training (Ausbildung), continuing education, retraining, and workforce upskilling. The product pairs curriculum-aligned content (including IHK-aligned vocational tracks) with an AI-powered learning assistant, trainer/learning-management tooling, and the ability for organizations to upload custom content. It counts 750+ corporate clients such as Deutsche Bahn, Bosch, and Vodafone. Simpleclub maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source Flutter tooling (math keyboard, flutter_math, design-token builder) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this profile is an end-user/EdTech company record rather than an API provider.

companies.name: BetterUp
companies.description: BetterUp is an enterprise Human Transformation Platform that combines human and AI-powered coaching, grounded in behavioral science and enterprise data, to help organizations develop leaders, managers, and their broader workforce. Founded by Alexi Robichaux, BetterUp serves 750+ enterprise customers including Google, Salesforce, Moderna, and Workday, with a network of 4,000+ coaches across 70+ countries. The platform delivers leadership development, manager effectiveness, AI coaching, and workforce resilience programs. BetterUp is HR-tech / organizational-development software and exposes no public developer API; platform integration is delivered through packaged enterprise connectors (Workday, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Viva, SAP SuccessFactors, Degreed) plus HRIS and SSO provisioning. Sector: hr-tech.

companies.name: Covalent
companies.description: Covalent (Covalent Networks) is a workforce operations software company for industrial manufacturing teams in the aerospace & defense and automotive sectors, with Fortune 500 manufacturing clients including Boeing. Its platform connects workforce skills, task execution and production data to digitize on-the-job training, capability and skills management, intelligent work allocation, workforce scheduling, and workflow automation with audit reporting, replacing paper-based shop-floor processes. Covalent exposes a GraphQL API and bidirectional integrations to move workforce, skills and production data across enterprise systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, UKG, Microsoft, and LMS/ERP/MES platforms. API access is authenticated with AWS Cognito (OAuth2/OIDC with MFA) and provisioned per tenant. The company is headquartered in Boston, MA and is backed by Felicis.

companies.name: EvolveApp INC.
companies.description: EvolveApp INC. (Evolve) is an AI-native enablement and performance platform for corporate learning and workforce training. Its product suite spans the Evolve LMS for courses, learning paths and branded academies; Evolve Generate for AI-powered course creation from raw materials; Evolve Studio for advanced authoring; an Assessment Center for skills and behavioral evaluation; an AI Knowledge Base instant-answer engine; and AI-driven Simulations for job-critical practice. Evolve serves 100+ enterprise clients and 2.9M+ learners worldwide, is SOC 2 (Type 1 and 2), ISO 27001 and GDPR compliant, and offers iOS and Android apps. The company is backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Panorama Education
companies.description: Panorama Education is a K-12 education technology company whose student success platform is used by thousands of school districts to turn student data into action across academics and behavior (MTSS/RTI), universal screening, social- emotional learning (SEL) and survey instruments, attendance, graduation planning, and family and staff engagement. The platform ingests data nightly from 24+ student information systems, learning management systems, and 100+ benchmark and state assessments using the OneRoster standard and secure file transfer. Panorama does not publish a public self-service developer API; integrations are delivered as managed B2B data synchronization. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 attested, 1EdTech Data Privacy certified, ESSA Level II/IV rated, and a Student Privacy Pledge signatory (FERPA/COPPA/PPRA/CCPA aligned).

companies.name: Ulysses (Kaminashi)
companies.description: Kaminashi Inc. (株式会社カミナシ) is a Tokyo-based SaaS company founded in December 2016 under its former corporate name Ulysses Inc. (ユリシーズ株式会社). It builds the Kaminashi frontline-operations DX platform for deskless workers — digital checklists and inspections, equipment maintenance (CMMS), frontline employee management, training and manuals, and reporting — serving food manufacturing, machine manufacturing, logistics, hotels, and building maintenance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and a16z. The company is ISMS (ISO/IEC 27001) certified and publishes no public developer API surface as of July 2026.

companies.name: OCLC
companies.description: The Discovery API allows you to surface both WorldCat and WorldCat Discovery central index data in search results, including: Materials held by your library and ...

companies.name: Tadeus API
companies.description: Tadeus is an AI voice agent platform that interviews your workforce in real voice, acts on what it hears, and returns structured records into existing systems. The public Integration API lets you create interview templates and campaigns, invite participants, and retrieve transcripts, structured results, and AI insights programmatically.

companies.name: Civitas Learning
companies.description: Civitas Learning is a higher education technology company whose Student Impact Platform unifies student data, predictive analytics, and coordinated workflows to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, persistence, and completion outcomes. The platform consolidates data from SIS, LMS, CRM, and event systems into a data lakehouse, layers institution-specific predictive models (CivIQ) on top, and surfaces real-time, actionable insights to advisors, faculty, and administrators through products such as Explore, Inspire, Impact, Illume, College Scheduler, Degree Map, and Academic Planning. Civitas Learning serves institutions of all sizes and pairs its software with strategic advisory services. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public operational, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Effectful
companies.description: Effectful Technologies is the company behind Effect, an open-source ecosystem of production-grade TypeScript libraries. The flagship `effect` library is a composable standard library and execution engine that unifies error handling, resource management, concurrency, dependency injection, observability, schema, and testability, letting developers focus on what a program should accomplish rather than how. Effect is positioned as "Layer 0" of a broader vision extending into distributed systems — RPC, SQL, clustering, AI integrations, and durable execution. The ecosystem ships as first-party npm packages under the `effect` and `@effect/*` scopes (MIT licensed) from the Effect-TS GitHub organization. Effectful is developer-tooling / library company, not an HTTP API provider, and is backed by Amplify Partners.

companies.name: Spring Health
companies.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

companies.name: Tobii
companies.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

companies.name: Lalilo
companies.description: Lalilo is an adaptive reading and literacy web application for primary-school classrooms, founded in Paris in 2016 and acquired by Renaissance (Wisconsin Rapids, USA) in 2021. It delivers roughly 90,000 interactive phonics, fluency and comprehension exercises that adapt in real time to each student, uses speech recognition to assess oral reading aloud, and gives teachers a dashboard for tracking progress and running differentiated small-group instruction. It is used by around 40,000 teachers and 400,000 students a year in France across cycles 2 and 3, with explicit support for DYS, allophone, ULIS, SEGPA and IME learners. Lalilo publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation: the product is consumed through the teacher and student web applications at app.lalilo.com, and integration or rostering questions are handled through Renaissance support rather than a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: UpCodes
companies.description: UpCodes is a comprehensive compliance and product research platform for the construction industry, offering a searchable database of US construction and building codes consolidated by state and city for easier navigation. The platform includes libraries of codes, diagrams, and assemblies, project collaboration and bookmarking, code calculators with a BIM design data import tool, SAML single sign-on for enterprise teams, and an AI Copilot that answers code compliance questions, locates assemblies, and generates project-specific checklists. Plans span Essentials, Professional, and Enterprise tiers. UpCodes does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Khan Academy
companies.description: Khan Academy is a non-profit providing free online educational content. The legacy Khan Academy API (v1) is deprecated/limited and the public api-explorer.khanacademy.org redirects to the main site. Some endpoints under www.khanacademy.org/api/v1/ remain in use for internal apps and historical integrations, but Khan Academy no longer maintains a publicly supported developer program.

companies.name: Ruzuku
companies.description: Ruzuku is a hosted online course platform for coaches, authors, and subject matter experts to create, teach, and sell online courses and learning communities. Ruzuku does not publish a documented public REST API or developer program. Its programmatic surface is exposed exclusively through a Zapier integration - authenticated with an API Key, API Secret, and Site URL generated under Account then Integrations then Configure Zapier - that offers event triggers (enrollments, lesson and course completions, quiz and assignment submissions, comments, cancellations) and a small set of student enroll, unenroll, and lookup actions. The APIs modeled below are honest logical groupings of that Zapier-mediated surface, not endpoints from a public Ruzuku API reference.

companies.name: Campus
companies.description: Campus (campus.edu) is an accredited, for-profit online community college offering associate degree programs built on the CUNY ASAP high-touch support model, with live classes taught by faculty from top universities, personal success coaching, and tuition capped at the Pell Grant maximum. Founded by Tade Oyerinde and backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Bloomberg Beta, 8VC, Rethink Education and others, Campus focuses on affordable, accessible higher education and career preparation across programs such as applied AI, business, information technology and healthcare administration. This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web surface; Campus is a consumer education provider and publishes no public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Classera
companies.description: Classera is an AI-powered education technology company that goes beyond a traditional Learning Management System (LMS) to deliver a complete education ecosystem spanning LMS, school ERP, fintech and payment solutions, and an educational marketplace, with more than 25 integrated services. Its platform emphasizes gamification, personalization, AI-driven and social learning, and serves K-12 private schools, higher education, ministries of education, and corporate and government training. Classera reports more than 30 million users across 45+ countries and partners including Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, HP, Zoom, and Intel. Headquartered in San Francisco, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Play Versus
companies.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Real Estate Institute of Australia
companies.description: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA), founded in 1924 and based in Canberra, is the national federation of the eight state and territory Real Estate Institutes (REINSW, REIV, REIQ, REIWA, REISA, REIT, REIACT, REINT), which between them represent roughly 85% of Australian real estate businesses and agents. REIA is a policy, research and accreditation body, not an operator of market infrastructure: it administers the REIA National Principles of Conduct that underpin state institute codes and training, awards Associate (AREI) and Fellow accreditations, runs the Australasian Auctioneering Championships (AUSTROS) jointly with REINZ and the National Awards for Excellence (NAFE), makes submissions to the Commonwealth Government, and publishes the quarterly Housing Affordability Report (HAR) and Real Estate Market Facts (REMF) series that Federal Treasury, the Reserve Bank, state treasuries and investment banks subscribe to. It sits well above the transaction rail in the Australian value chain - listings run through REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain, settlement through PEXA, valuation through PropTrack and CoreLogic, and title through the state land registries - and REIA touches none of those pipes. Its API posture is therefore an honest absence: no developer portal, no API subdomain, no OpenAPI or OData contract, and no RESO reference anywhere on its estate, because RESO is a NAR-mandated United States construct with no Australian counterpart. What REIA sells is data, not access to it - the HAR and REMF reports are AUD 450 subscriptions and each of the 7 HAR and 15 REMF underlying datasets is a separate AUD 280 subscription, delivered as documents through a platformOS/Insites ecommerce storefront with Stripe checkout behind an email-and-password account. Policy submissions, standalone research reports and the strategic plan are freely downloadable PDFs; the quarterly numbers are not, and there is no open data.

companies.name: ClassWallet
companies.description: ClassWallet is a patented digital wallet and public-funds disbursement platform used by government agencies, school districts, and program administrators to distribute, control, and reconcile public money. Recipients access and spend allocated funds online or in-store while administrators get spending controls, approved marketplaces, reimbursement workflows, direct vendor payments (DirectPay), and audit-ready reporting and compliance. ClassWallet powers K-12 education programs, Education Savings Accounts (ESAs), scholarships and grants, government assistance, and vocational rehabilitation initiatives. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes product and program surfaces but no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Cometa
companies.description: Cometa (getcometa.com / cometaedu.com) is a Mexican education technology company that provides an operating system for private schools. More than 500 private schools in Mexico use Cometa to run and automate their operations across a set of integrated modules: Cobranzas (tuition collections with WhatsApp and email payment reminders and dashboards), Tienda en linea (an online store for uniforms, materials and services with vendor management), Admisiones y Reinscripciones (admissions and re-enrollment workflows), Comunicaciones (AI-assisted, multi-channel family communications with engagement analytics), Calificaciones (grade entry and SEP-compliant report cards and digital credentials), and Gestion Escolar (attendance, incident logging and administrative workflows). Cometa is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was surfaced as a stub in the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Cometa publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

companies.name: Imperfect
companies.description: Imperfect (Imperfect Wellness, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) consumer startup building an adaptive AI training coach for endurance athletes across cycling, trail running, swimming, and other sports. The mobile app connects to a user's wearables and health apps to generate real-time training, recovery, and nutrition recommendations that adapt to how the athlete's body is actually responding day to day, rather than following a static plan written weeks in advance. Founded by Matin Tamizi (previously built and sold two fintech companies and authored a widely used open-source Garmin library used by Stanford Health). Imperfect ships as a consumer mobile application (Google Play) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Parallel Learning
companies.description: Parallel Learning is a special education services and staffing platform that connects K-12 schools and districts with a nationwide network of licensed clinicians for the remote delivery of specialized student support. Through its proprietary, HIPAA/FERPA-compliant Pathway platform it delivers virtual psychoeducational and neurodevelopmental assessments, speech-language therapy, behavioral and mental-health counseling, specialized instruction in reading, writing, and math, and executive-function coaching, pairing secure teletherapy with progress tracking and clinical oversight so districts can meet compliance requirements and improve student outcomes. The company serves thousands of students across dozens of states and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Pensive
companies.description: Pensive is an AI grading platform for educators at schools and universities. Its "AI Grader" helps instructors evaluate student work — grading assignments and returning feedback at scale — alongside an AI tutor product for students. Pensive serves distinct teacher, student, and administrator surfaces, publishes case studies with university instructors, and maintains a SOC 2 trust center. It is a seed-stage company backed by Mayfield. As of this profiling Pensive operates a private, authenticated web product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Wited (Portal Educativo)
companies.description: Wited (formerly Portal Educativo) is a Chilean edtech company backed by 500 Global that delivers online academic support and homeschooling across Latin America. Its two products - Reforzamiento (tutoring, homework help, and exam prep for K-12 students in traditional schools) and Colegio Online (a complete online school for homeschoolers) - combine curriculum-aligned courses, interactive exercises, the Max AI tutoring chatbot, live teacher support (Profes Express), and a parent progress dashboard. Wited operates in Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Panama, Argentina, Brazil, Spain, and the United States. The consumer platform runs at app.wited.com against a private backend (api.wited.com); the company publishes no public developer program or API.

companies.name: Coachup
companies.description: CoachUp is the nation's leading private sports coaching marketplace, founded in 2012 in Boston by Jordan Fliegel, Arian Radmand, and Gabe Durazo. It connects athletes of all levels — and the parents of young athletes — with vetted, background-checked private and small-group coaches across basketball, soccer, football, baseball, running and track and field, volleyball, swimming, softball, tennis, lacrosse, fitness, and dance. Coaches are discoverable by sport and location, sessions average $40–$60 per hour, and every session is backed by $1 million liability insurance. The platform has hosted more than 13,000 coaches serving over 100,000 athletes, with Boston, New York, Los Angeles, Dallas, and Chicago among its top training markets. CoachUp is backed by General Catalyst, Point Judith Capital, and Techstars. As of this profile CoachUp exposes only a consumer web and mobile experience with no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: 3P Learning Pty
companies.description: 3P Learning is an educational technology company that builds blended learning software for mathematics and literacy used by schools and families worldwide. Its product family includes Mathletics, Mathseeds, Reading Eggs, Writing Legends, LiteracyPlanet and Brightpath, reaching more than 20 million students across 130+ countries. The programs pair interactive student activities with teacher dashboards, reporting and curriculum-aligned content, and integrate into school systems via single sign-on and rostering standards such as Clever and LTI. 3P Learning is backed by Insight Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network. This company publishes consumer and school-facing web and mobile products but does not expose a public first-party developer API or documented API surface.

companies.name: Atom Learning
companies.description: Atom Learning is a UK edtech company providing an online, adaptive exam-preparation and learning platform for children aged 7 to 16. Its consumer product, Atom Home, delivers personalised practice, unlimited mock tests with instant marking, and progress tracking for 11+ grammar and independent-school entrance exams (GL, CEM, CSSE, ISEB), CAT4, Key Stage 2 SATs, and GCSE revision. Its schools product, Atom School, gives teachers curriculum-mapped resources and assessment tools and is used by over 1,000 schools. Founded by educators and assessment specialists, Atom has supported hundreds of thousands of families as a lower-cost alternative to private tutoring. The company was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer web/app product surface but no public developer API.

companies.name: Blomma
companies.description: Blomma is an AI-powered career coaching platform that pairs artificial intelligence with emotional intelligence to act as a private thinking partner for professionals. Through chat-based coaching, guided reflection, goal-setting with built-in accountability, a personal journal, and a growth dashboard, Blomma helps founders, people leaders, and ambitious professionals turn abstract aspirations into concrete, trackable goals, and can personalize coaching from uploaded performance reviews and development plans. It is delivered as a consumer subscription through web and mobile apps, with custom team plans for organizations, and does not currently expose a public developer API.

companies.name: Bloom Institute of Technology
companies.description: Bloom Institute of Technology (formerly Lambda School) is an online coding bootcamp founded in 2017 that trains learners for AI-driven tech careers through part-time and full-time programs in Full Stack Web Development, Backend Development, and Data Science, plus corporate "AI for Developer Productivity" training. It is known for its income-share and deferred-tuition model ($0 upfront with a job-contingent payment plan) and a tuition-refund guarantee. The company reports 4,000+ graduates since 2017. It is a venture-backed consumer education company (backed by GV) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Capella University
companies.description: Capella University is an accredited online university owned by Strategic Education, Inc. (SEI), offering competency-based bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees plus graduate certificates across business, counseling and therapy, education, health sciences, information technology, nursing, psychology, and social work. Capella is regionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and delivers coursework through two learning formats — FlexPath, a self-paced competency-based model, and GuidedPath, a structured-timeline model — serving working adults and professional learners entirely online.

companies.name: Clanbeat
companies.description: Clanbeat is an Estonian education-technology company whose app supports student and staff well-being by nurturing social and emotional learning (SEL) through co-creation. The platform provides well-being tracking, quality reflections, meaningful connections between students and educators, and tools to co-create SEL curriculum. It is used by international schools, educators, students, and fitness and lifelong-learning communities to evidence group emotional well-being and bring classes closer together. Clanbeat is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application at app.clanbeat.com; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or partner integration surface at this time.

companies.name: Complori
companies.description: Complori is a Berlin, Germany based online education company that teaches children and young people to code through live, small-group video classes led by qualified coaches in a protected digital space. Its programs span programming with Minecraft, Python, JavaScript game development, app development, and financial literacy, backed by a learning platform with challenges and exercises, a mobile learning app, completion certificates, flexible family-friendly scheduling, and holiday camps. Complori operates a B2C consumer education service (with parents as the decision-makers) rather than a developer-facing API product, and runs an education scholarship program to broaden access across socioeconomic backgrounds. Backed by Speedinvest.

companies.name: creativeLIVE
companies.description: creativeLIVE (CreativeLive) is an online learning platform offering more than 2,300 on-demand courses and live interactive classes taught by working professionals across photography, video and filmmaking, graphic and web design, business and entrepreneurship, arts and crafts, audio and music production, and AI and technology. Learners access practical, skill-based instruction through a subscription, with certificates of completion available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; creativeLIVE exposes no public developer API, but does publish a machine-readable llms.txt course index for AI agents.

companies.name: DIY
companies.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

companies.name: Geniebook
companies.description: Geniebook is a Singapore-based educational technology company (Geniebook Pte Ltd, incorporated 2016) offering an AI-powered online learning platform for primary, secondary, and JC students. Its product suite includes GenieSmart (AI-personalised worksheets generated from a library of 300,000+ MOE syllabus-aligned questions, using algorithms co-developed with A*STAR), GenieClass (live and recorded online classes taught by experienced teachers), and GenieAsk (real-time moderated teacher chats for after-school academic support), plus a CAMPUS physical-tutoring offering and PSLE/JC preparation programmes. Geniebook serves more than 220,000 students across Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer (B2C) learning application delivered via web and mobile apps; no public developer API is published.

companies.name: GenM
companies.description: GenM (now operating as Acadium) is a digital marketing career and apprenticeship platform that connects emerging marketers with mentors and businesses. The platform offers free digital marketing courses (SEO, social media, email, and content marketing), hands-on MicroTasks for portfolio building, three-month remote apprenticeships, and Acadium Plus, an eight-week program that leads to full-time hiring. Businesses use Acadium to crowdsource marketing work and mentor emerging talent while growing their operations. GenM was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company operates a consumer/business web application at app.acadium.com and publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Gnowbe
companies.description: Gnowbe is an AI-powered workforce enablement and performance platform for enterprise learning, enablement, and alignment. It turns static content and communication into mobile-first microlearning experiences with AI-powered activation and execution tracking, so teams do not just learn but perform. Trusted by 500,000+ learners across 100+ countries, Gnowbe combines authoring, AI content creation, group-based delivery, completion and engagement analytics, and integrations (SSO/SAML, LMS/SCORM, xAPI/LRS, HR systems, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Zapier's 5,000+ tools). Gnowbe is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

companies.name: GoPillar
companies.description: GoPillar (operated by CoContest Italy Srl, Rome, Italy) is a crowdsourced architectural and interior design marketplace where homeowners, businesses, and small construction firms launch online design contests and receive dozens of proposals from a global community of 70,000+ registered architects and designers. Clients set a project timeline, brief the community, message participating designers, and select the winning concept, with follow-on one-to-one and offline executive-project services. GoPillar also runs GoPillar Academy, an e-learning platform offering professional BIM, 3D, and design courses plus custom corporate training for architecture and construction firms. GoPillar is a consumer/SMB web platform and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Home From College
companies.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

companies.name: Interintellect
companies.description: Interintellect is the world's leading salon platform, a creator-led cultural center for intellectual conversation founded in March 2019 by art philosopher Anna Gat. The platform lets people attend and host high-quality salons and discussions online and offline, across philosophy, technology, poetry, history, and the arts, building community around shared intellectual interests. It supports independent thinkers and hosts through ticket revenue, training, and a peer community, with paid membership tiers granting event access, members-only sessions, community forums, and global in-person gatherings. Interintellect is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; it publishes no public API or developer platform, so this profile carries identity and website-property signals rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: KiwiCo
companies.description: KiwiCo, Inc. is a direct-to-consumer education company headquartered in Mountain View, California, founded in 2011 by Sandra Oh Lin. KiwiCo designs and ships hands-on STEAM (science, technology, engineering, art and math) project kits — branded as crates — on a monthly subscription, with distinct lines aimed at every age from infants through teens and adults, alongside single-purchase kits sold through its online store. A KiwiCo Education division supplies the same project kits and NGSS-aligned lesson guides to schools, homeschools, after-school programs and camps. KiwiCo operates as a consumer e-commerce and subscription business and publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, CLI or webhook surface, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents on any of its hosts. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and public web properties only.

companies.name: Liveboard
companies.description: LiveBoard is a tutor-management platform that helps tutoring businesses, academies, and independent tutors run their operations end to end. It combines branded virtual classrooms (video calls, screen sharing, an interactive whiteboard, recording, and file sharing) with session scheduling and attendance tracking, tutor/student/parent management, calendar-based billing with online payments, auto-invoicing, payroll, and progress reporting. Liveboard says it serves 200,000+ tutors and companies across 200+ countries, scaling from solo tutors to organizations with thousands of tutors. It is a consumer/SaaS product with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time; integrations are teaching-focused (Wacom pen tablets, a LaTeX formula editor, and the Desmos graphing calculator). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Melodics
companies.description: Melodics is a New Zealand-based interactive music-learning application that teaches drums, MIDI keyboards, and pad controllers (finger drumming) through gamified, real-time lessons. It connects to electronic instruments and MIDI controllers to give immediate feedback on timing and accuracy, offering guided learning paths, song tutorials, and structured daily practice for beginner through advanced players across desktop and mobile. Melodics is a consumer edtech product and a portfolio company of 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Nookly
companies.description: Nookly is a personalized children's content platform that helps the adults who care for a child — parents, teachers, therapists, and early-childhood organizations — turn their intimate knowledge of that child into custom stories, songs, visual schedules, social stories, emotion cards, and behavior supports. Grounded in social-emotional learning and behavioral science, it produces developmentally appropriate, COPPA/FERPA-compliant content for children ages 2-11, with particular value for neurodivergent kids (autism, ADHD, speech delays, anxiety, and sensory processing differences). Used across homes, classrooms, and clinics in 50+ states.

companies.name: Simbel
companies.description: Simbel is a Paris-based HR technology company (founded 2021, backed by Speedinvest) offering a smart, unified training management suite that combines a Training Management System (TMS) and a Learning Management System (LMS) in one platform. It helps HR and L&D teams automate the full training lifecycle, from need assessment and request approvals through session organization, e-learning delivery, real-time reporting, and legal compliance (BPF, Qualiopi, BDES). Simbel connects to major HRIS and learning tools such as Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, ADP, Lucca, Payfit, BambooHR, 360Learning, and Docebo through pre-built integrations. As of this enrichment pass Simbel publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connectors rather than a self-serve public API.

companies.name: Smore
companies.description: Smore is a newsletter and flyer builder purpose-built for educators, schools, and districts, letting teachers and administrators create accessible, mobile-friendly digital newsletters from customizable templates to keep families and staff informed. The product emphasizes WCAG AA accessibility, translation for multilingual families, and engagement analytics on opens and clicks. Smore is now part of SchoolStatus, the family-engagement platform. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Smore publishes no public developer program, API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface — this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture only.

companies.name: Solvely Ai
companies.description: Solvely is an all-in-one AI study platform for students from K-12 through graduate level, trusted by more than 10 million students across 5,000+ universities worldwide. It combines multi-model homework help with step-by-step solutions, an AI note taker that transcribes lectures into structured notes, a quiz maker, an essay writer, math and equation solvers (algebra, geometry, calculus, statistics), auto-generated flashcards and study guides, mock exams, an exam predictor, and cheat sheets. Solvely is available on the web, iOS, Android, and as a Chrome/Edge browser extension, with free and paid (Solvely Unlimited) tiers. It is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Track Titan
companies.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

companies.name: Tynker
companies.description: Tynker is a coding platform for kids and teens ages 5-18 that makes it fun to learn programming through game-based, interactive courses, with students starting in visual block-based coding and progressing to real-world languages like Python and JavaScript. The platform powers the creativity of over 100 million students and serves thousands of schools and educators worldwide, spanning home plans for parents, K-12 school curriculum, Hour of Code activities, and Minecraft modding. Tynker is a 500 Global and Felicis portfolio company, now part of CodeHS, and publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Vector Solutions
companies.description: Vector Solutions is a SaaS provider of industry-specific training, operational readiness, workforce management, and risk-management software. Its portfolio spans Learning Management Systems (LMS), Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) management, staff scheduling, incident and equipment tracking, professional development and evaluation management, and large online course libraries. The company serves education (K-12 and higher ed), public safety (fire, EMS, law enforcement), government, manufacturing, construction, and gaming markets, helping organizations prepare their people, stay in compliance, and manage operational risk. Vector Solutions is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It runs a GraphQL endpoint at api.vectorsolutions.com/graphql that backs its applications; that endpoint is live but not publicly documented and has schema introspection disabled.

companies.name: Conceive
companies.description: Conceive is a telehealth platform for fertility and pregnancy support. It offers 24/7 text access to fertility and pregnancy nurses, coaches, and dietitians, personalized fertility coaching, fertility test interpretation, virtual video visits with providers, expert-led community events, and an educational library. Membership is delivered through Conceive Plus and Conceive Premium tiers. The company is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. As a consumer telehealth app it publishes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its published identity and domain security posture.

companies.name: Cvent Community
companies.description: Cvent Community is Cvent's customer support, knowledge base, certification, and peer-to-peer forum hub at community.cvent.com. It is the 24/7 destination where event professionals learn Cvent products, search the Knowledge Base, take Cvent Academy training and certification courses, and exchange best practices with other users through Open Forum and product-specific learning centers (Attendee Hub, Registration, OnArrival, Surveys, Cvent Supplier Network, Event Diagramming, Cvent Studio, Cvent Webinar, Passkey). Cvent Community is not itself an API product; programmatic access to Cvent data is delivered via the Cvent Platform REST API at api-platform.cvent.com using OAuth 2.0 client credentials.

companies.name: Ethos Systems
companies.description: Ethos Systems is an AI-powered human readiness platform that unifies learning, performance, and outcomes management in a single system built for enterprise and government deployment across both commercial and classified networks. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Ethos delivers personalized training with algorithm-driven interventions, rapid AI content development, and real-time readiness dashboards that connect learning to operational outcomes. It serves the U.S. military, federal civilian agencies, life sciences, manufacturing, freight and logistics, hospitality, athletics, utilities, insurance, and government contractors, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the Westly Group, and Pear VC. The company operates the Ethos and Learn to Win platforms; its developer and product documentation is gated behind authentication and it exposes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Poppins
companies.description: Poppins is a French digital health company that develops a clinically validated digital therapeutic (DTx) for children aged 7-11 with dyslexia. Classified as a Class I medical device under EU Regulation 2017/745, the mobile application delivers home-based, game-based training sessions of about 20 minutes per day, 3-5 times per week, targeting phonological awareness, reading speed, and visual attention span. Poppins complements in-person speech therapy, supports speech-language pathologists through professional accounts, and partners with insurers. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Poppins publishes a consumer and healthcare-professional web/mobile product but no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: Branchtrack
companies.description: BranchTrack is a browser-based authoring platform for building interactive branching scenarios and conversation simulations used in corporate learning and development. Instructional designers and L&D teams create decision-tree simulations with no coding or design skills, then deploy them inside existing LMS platforms or embed them into courses authored in Articulate Storyline, Rise, Adobe Captivate, Gomo, and Lectora. Simulations export as SCORM and xAPI (Tin Can) packages and can be shared as responsive, mobile-native experiences with learner analytics and completion tracking. BranchTrack is a portfolio company of Seedcamp. The platform exposes no first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; third-party embedding is available via the Embedly oEmbed provider, and LMS delivery via SCORM/xAPI.

companies.name: Conicle
companies.description: Conicle is a Thai education-technology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bangkok that offers an all-in-one corporate learning platform (ConicleX) letting organizations build, assign, and track online courses, in-house training, and skill-development pathways for their employees. The cloud-based learning management system serves more than 50 leading enterprises — including Honda, Coca-Cola, Unilever, McDonald's, Sansiri, and The Mall — and over one million learners across the banking, retail, healthcare, energy, insurance, and consumer-product sectors. Conicle has raised Series A funding led by InVent (the corporate venture arm of Intouch Holdings), with backing from 500 Global and Stormbreaker Ventures. Conicle publishes a shared design-system web-components library used across its properties but does not currently expose a public developer API.

companies.name: Fiveable
companies.description: Fiveable is an Advanced Placement (AP) exam preparation platform covering all 38 AP subjects. It provides study guides, unit-organized subject review hubs, practice questions modeled on real AP exam formats, AI-scored free-response questions (FRQs), cheatsheets, key-term glossaries, and AP score calculators that predict likely exam outcomes. Fiveable serves three audiences - secondary students cramming and reviewing for AP exams, teachers seeking classroom and assessment materials, and schools needing district-wide exam-prep support. The platform blends traditional study resources with AI-powered scoring and feedback. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Fiveable publishes a consumer web application but no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: grasp
companies.description: Grasp is a members-based, AI-powered learning platform based in London, England that builds personalized, AI-curated short courses. Learners discuss a goal with an AI mentor, which co-creates a syllabus and assembles a structured "learning path" from the clearest, most credible resources on the web - organized into focused, roughly hour-long lessons with clear outcomes and practice exercises. Grasp is delivered as a client-rendered React single-page app with a 14-day free trial and a single monthly membership; a selection of public courses and lessons is browsable without an account, and a sister product, Grasp Concepts, lives at concepts.grasp.study. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and point-nine.

companies.name: Gronda
companies.description: Gronda is a professional community and learning platform for chefs and hospitality professionals, offering 70+ masterclasses and 20,000+ exclusive restaurant recipes from leading chefs, a chef directory and creator program, and team and culinary-school plans. Members share culinary creations, follow world-class chefs, and access PRO subscription content through the Gronda web and mobile apps. Backed by Speedinvest, Gronda was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; it is a consumer/community product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Multiverse
companies.description: Multiverse is a British education-technology company (founded 2016 by Euan Blair and Sophie Adelman, headquartered in London) that operates an AI-adoption and workforce-upskilling platform. It delivers apprenticeships and training programmes in AI, data, software engineering, and digital skills, pairing on-the-job learning with expert coaching so employers can close skills gaps and build future-ready teams. Backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and StepStone Group, Multiverse serves enterprise clients across the UK and US. The company exposes no public developer API; its digital surface is a marketing site, a learner/employer login, a help centre, a community hub, a blog, a service status page, and a trust centre.

companies.name: WizerMe
companies.description: WizerMe (Wizer) is an edtech platform used by more than 700,000 teachers to build interactive, self-grading digital worksheets. Educators turn existing PDFs and documents into engaging assessments with multiple-choice, video, audio, open-response, and puzzle question types, record video or audio instructions, apply differentiation rules, monitor student work in real time, schedule availability and time limits, and sync grades with Google Classroom. Students submit answers as text, audio, or video. Wizer offers a free tier (Wizer Create) and a premium tier (Wizer Boost) plus school and district plans, and is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface is currently published.

companies.name: Lica
companies.description: Lica is an AI research company building a substrate to train and evaluate AI models to be capable design partners across expressions of taste and consumption. Its research spans spatial reasoning and composition, layout generation and editing, vector-graphics (SVG) understanding, personalization and brand identity, and animation generation. Lica publishes the LICA dataset of layered graphic-design compositions and GDB (Graphic Design Benchmark), a real-world benchmark that scores frontier models on designer workflows across layout, typography, infographics, template semantics and animation. The company is backed by Accel, South Park Commons and Village Global. As of July 2026 Lica ships no public API, developer portal or API reference; product access is an email waitlist and its public developer surface is the lica-world GitHub organization, including the first-party DesignMCP MCP server.

companies.name: Outschool
companies.description: Outschool is an education-technology marketplace for live, small-group online classes for learners ages 3-18. It connects families and independent teachers across 140,000+ subjects — from math and coding to art, music, and hobbies — offered as one-time sessions, ongoing courses, camps, and social clubs delivered over live video. Outschool also serves schools and districts through its for-organizations program. Backed by Bond Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures, and Y Combinator, the platform is a consumer web application; it exposes no publicly documented developer API.
