The site is powered by an internal, undocumented GraphQL endpoint (outschool.com/graphql) used only by its own front end and largely blocked to crawlers. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record enriched from the provider's public web surface.

companies.name: Showbie
companies.description: Showbie is a K-12 learning platform for iPad that streamlines teaching workflows across assignments, feedback, grading, and classroom communication for teachers, students, and parents. Backed by Point Nine, it combines a digital classroom, annotation and file-sharing tools, and messaging into a single app used by schools worldwide. Showbie exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs surface; this profile captures the company's public web, support, compliance, privacy, and terms properties, plus a live domain security probe.

companies.name: Lateral
companies.description: Lateral was a Berlin- and Hobart-based AI research software company founded in 2013 that built machine-learning powered content recommendation and document navigation tools. Its early product was a conceptual text-matching and recommendation API that let developers insert documents and retrieve semantically similar content, with pre-populated corpora covering arXiv, PubMed, Wikipedia, news and SEC filings. The company later pivoted to an LLM-assisted research workspace for navigating information across large document sets, and published open-source research on hyperbolic-space word embeddings (Poincare embeddings, hyperplane hashers, WARP recommenders). Lateral was permanently shut down on 26 June 2025; the team pointed users to a successor open-source research platform at coordination.network. The public API, its documentation host and the application host are all retired, so this profile documents a historical API surface and the client libraries that remain published.

companies.name: Torch
companies.description: Torch (Redfish Labs, Inc. dba Torch Leadership Labs) is a leadership development and executive coaching platform that pairs expert human coaches with AI to help mid-market and enterprise organizations grow leaders and navigate change. Its offerings include Change Coaching (leaders-turned-coaches trained in Torch's change approach), the Spark AI coaching agent (always-on AI guidance for practicing conversations and turning insight into progress), and Organizational Intelligence (real-time visibility into change patterns and people dynamics). Torch focuses on AI transformation, organizational restructuring, organizational resilience, and leadership growth, and counts Airbnb, Reddit, Tripadvisor, FICO, and Twitch among its customers. Torch is a SaaS product with SSO (SAML), Zoom, and Slack integrations but publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

companies.name: Sunlight
companies.description: Sunlight is an educational-spending platform that lets organizations fund learning for their people. Administrators create groups, invite registered or unregistered members, allocate a per-user education budget ("sunlight"), and let members place orders for courses, books and subscriptions from providers such as Amazon and Platzi, while an activity feed tracks what members join and buy. Its REST API is built on the JSON:API specification (media type application/vnd.api+json) with Bearer-token authentication, and exposes groups, group membership and invitations, per-user credit/budget transactions, orders, and activities. Sunlight was backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest.

companies.name: CircuitLab
companies.description: CircuitLab, Inc. is an in-browser schematic capture and circuit simulation platform that lets engineers, students, educators, and hobbyists design and analyze analog and digital electronics systems before building a physical prototype. Running entirely in the browser with no installation, it offers schematic capture, mixed-signal SPICE-style simulation (DC, AC, transient, frequency-domain), custom device models and symbols, expression-based parameters, and shareable, exportable documentation. CircuitLab also publishes an electronics curriculum (CircuitLab Academy, the Ultimate Electronics textbook), community forums, and an electronics Q&A. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Y Combinator. At the time of this enrichment pass CircuitLab publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API description, so this profile captures its public web identity only.

companies.name: Edyoucated
companies.description: Edyoucated is a German SaaS company offering an AI-powered corporate learning and skills-management platform for mid-to-large enterprises. The product combines a learning management / learning experience system (central management of training, mandatory compliance training, seminar administration, AI-assisted content creation, blended learning, and learning analytics) with skills management (skill cataloging, assessments, gap analysis, expert identification, and career guidance) to give organizations a common language for skills and personalized learning pathways. It also offers consulting for custom skill-taxonomy development. Customers include Deutsche Bahn, BASF, Shopware, and Finanz Informatik. Edyoucated is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer/API surface, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation.

companies.name: MedAll
companies.description: MedAll is a UK-founded healthcare education platform on a mission to make medical education radically accessible. It hosts live and on-demand courses, conferences, workshops, webinars and training sessions for healthcare professionals, students and organisations, and provides event management tooling for registrations, feedback forms, certificates, abstracts, schedules and digital poster halls, alongside CME (continuing medical education), question banks and mobile apps for iOS and Android. The platform is used by clinicians and institutions worldwide. As of this enrichment pass MedAll publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture. Backed by Seedcamp.

companies.name: Brainly
companies.description: Brainly is an education technology company founded in 2009 in Krakow, Poland (originally Zadane.pl) and now headquartered in New York City. It operates the world's largest online learning and homework-help community, a gamified, crowdsourced social-learning network where students, parents, and teachers ask and answer academic questions with verified answers from peers, educators, and Brainly's proprietary AI. As of 2025 the platform serves over 350 million monthly users across roughly 35 countries and has evolved from a community Q&A product into an agentic AI Learning Companion spanning homework help, AI tutoring, test prep, and classroom participation. Brainly is a consumer subscription business (Brainly Plus); it publishes no official public developer API — this profile captures its public web, security, and policy surface.

companies.name: Bridgetown Research
companies.description: Bridgetown Research is an AI-powered research and analysis platform that helps organizations analyze businesses with speed and precision. Its AI agents conduct expert interviews, gather primary and secondary data at scale, and execute 300+ of the most common analyses to power autonomous market research and commercial due diligence. The platform serves private equity and venture capital firms, professional services firms, and corporate strategy and development teams, who access it either through a SOC 2-compliant SaaS platform with interactive generative-search reporting or via an email-driven workflow that returns PDF reports. Bridgetown Research also exposes a REST API (documented on Apidog at docs.bridgetownresearch.com) for creating research projects and managing experts, expert actions, and scheduled calls. It is backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

companies.name: Headspace
companies.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.

companies.name: Huron Consulting Group
companies.description: Huron Consulting Group is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Huron Consulting Group API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Meadow
companies.description: Meadow is a financial technology company delivering modern student financial services to colleges and universities. Its platform spans the full student financial lifecycle — Meadow Price (a mobile, SAI-compliant net price calculator), Meadow Pay (student billing and payments with automated workflows), Meadow Pre (pre-collections for recovering unpaid tuition), and Meadow Checkout (campus-wide collection of non-tuition fees). Meadow helps institutions improve enrollment, retention, and payment outcomes from application through graduation. Backed by Matrix Partners and Y Combinator. No public API or developer platform is published as of this profile.

companies.name: Tap
companies.description: TAP (Training All People, Inc.) is a next-generation technician training platform for advanced and precision manufacturers. TAP combines online courses (pneumatics, electrical fundamentals, robotics, safety, and semiconductor basics) with immersive VR simulations that replicate real factory equipment and procedures, plus in-simulation quizzes, VR scenario assessments, and workforce skills-profiling dashboards. The platform lets manufacturers evaluate, standardize, and upskill their technician workforce at scale while minimizing disruption to production. Customers include Northrop Grumman, ACC, SUNY, and Dallas College. Backed by 8vc and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; TAP currently publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Studocu
companies.description: Studocu (operated by StudeerSnel B.V., Amsterdam) is a global online learning platform and study-materials marketplace where students access, share, and upload course documents, lecture notes, summaries, and exam prep across thousands of institutions and subjects. The platform layers AI study tools on top of its crowdsourced document library — an Ask AI chat, AI Notes generation, and an AI Quiz Generator — alongside course organization, study lists, and a Premium subscription for unlimited downloads and full document access. Backed by Partech and Point Nine, Studocu was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public security, trust, and web-property surface.

companies.name: ApplyBoard
companies.description: ApplyBoard is a study-abroad application platform that simplifies the international education journey by connecting students, recruitment partners, and partner schools on a single platform. Students explore and apply to more than 1,500 global universities and colleges across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and Germany, with supporting services spanning financial products, English-language test vouchers, and accommodation. ApplyBoard also operates ApplyProof, a document-verification and trust product. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK; its programmatic surface (including ApplyProof) is partner-gated. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: ApplyBoard Inc.
companies.description: ApplyBoard Inc. is a Kitchener-Waterloo, Canada-based education technology company that operates one of the world's largest online platforms for international student recruitment. Its marketplace connects prospective students and recruitment partners with more than 1,500 educational institutions across Australia, Canada, Germany, Ireland, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and reports having helped over 1.5 million students apply to 150,000+ programs. Beyond the core application platform, ApplyBoard offers "360 Solutions" spanning language-test vouchers, financial services, and student loans, along with ApplyProof (a standalone document-verification service) and ApplyBoard Test Solutions. ApplyBoard does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: BridgeU
companies.description: BridgeU is an education technology company providing a university and careers guidance platform for international schools. Used by more than 1,200 partner schools across 150+ countries, the platform helps students from Grade 9 onward explore careers, research over 26,000 global universities, build shortlists, and manage applications in one connected system, with analytics dashboards for counsellors and AI-assisted guidance. BridgeU is a Seedcamp portfolio company and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface as of this enrichment pass; integration with school systems (for example ManageBac+) is handled via partner single sign-on rather than an openly documented API.

companies.name: Descomplica
companies.description: Descomplica is a Brazilian online education (edtech) company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, offering a digital learning platform for ENEM and vestibular exam prep, K-12 (Escolar), undergraduate and graduate (Pós-graduação) degrees, public-exam (Concursos) preparation, and corporate training. The platform delivers live and recorded classes, study plans, tutoring, exercises, and support materials to millions of Brazilian students, and is MEC-authorized. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company operates consumer and corporate learning products but does not publish a public developer API program.

companies.name: doinstruct
companies.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

companies.name: eSpark
companies.description: eSpark is a K-5 adaptive learning platform that extends a district's core reading and math programs with differentiated, standards-aligned practice in reading, math, and writing. The platform uses adaptive lesson sequencing that adjusts difficulty to each student's performance, interest-based content, and real-time feedback to deliver personalized instruction, and it reports back to teachers and administrators on student progress. eSpark serves 10,000+ schools and districts nationwide and rosters students through Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom, and QR-code sign-in. eSpark was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures company identity, its public web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: EverTrue
companies.description: EverTrue is a donor experience and fundraising platform for nonprofit, higher-education, and healthcare advancement teams, serving more than 13,000 teams. Its product suite spans AI-driven prospect identification and research (Signal, DonorSearch), donor outreach and stewardship (ThankView personalized video, Pledgemine direct mail), and endowment reporting (Balance, Impact, ODDER). EverTrue integrates with advancement CRMs such as Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT via an automated data sync. EverTrue operates as a closed B2B SaaS: it runs internal REST APIs behind its iOS, Android, and single-page web applications but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API program. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Techstars.

companies.name: Greator
companies.description: Greator (formerly GEDANKENtanken, founded 2012) is Germany's largest personal- development platform, headquartered in Cologne and serving roughly 234,000 customers. It runs a B2C ecosystem of free content (masterclasses, podcasts, a YouTube channel, magazine articles and personality tests) alongside paid, certified training programs such as The School of Life, Momentum Mastery, the Finance Academy and TheKey speaking training. Greator also produces live events including the annual Greator Festival (15,000+ attendees, 400+ speakers) and operates Greator Business, a B2B corporate offering. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Greator publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Mobilize
companies.description: Mobilize (mobilize.io) is a community and learning software platform purpose-built for associations and professional networks, now operating under the Forj brand (forj.ai). The platform unifies member community and continuing education in one place through its products Forj Connect (peer-to-peer and group member communication), Forj Learn (a learning management system for continuing education, certification, and social learning), and Journey by Forj (a combined community-and-learning experience). Mobilize was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a member/admin web application (app.mobilize.io) and a Zendesk help center but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so this profile carries verified company identity and link properties rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Rilla
companies.description: Rilla is an AI conversation-intelligence and coaching platform built for in-person and outside sales teams. Reps record their face-to-face customer conversations, and Rilla transcribes and analyzes them so managers can run virtual "ridealongs" and deliver targeted, data-driven coaching at scale. The platform surfaces talk patterns, objection handling, and outcome analytics across thousands of field conversations to help teams raise close rates, increase ticket size, and speed up rep ramp. Rilla is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the AI sector. As of this profile Rilla exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this record captures its public web identity and a domain-security probe.

companies.name: Sphero
companies.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

companies.name: edX
companies.description: edX is an online learning platform now operated by 2U; the underlying Open edX software is open source. Open edX exposes a comprehensive REST API surface (Enrollment, Courses, Users, Catalog, Discussion, Grades, LTI, Enterprise) and hosts a public API at api.edx.org for partners.

companies.name: Cambly
companies.description: Cambly is an online English-language learning platform, founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, that connects English learners in more than 190 countries with native-speaking tutors over on-demand video chat. Its consumer products include Cambly (adult learners), Cambly Kids (ages 4-15), Cambly Pro, and Cambly for Organizations/Business. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Y Combinator, the company operates a marketplace connecting students and tutors with weekly payouts. Cambly does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public company surface, GitHub organization, and domain-security posture.

companies.name: BridgeCare Finance
companies.description: BridgeCare (getbridgecare.com) is an integrated, modular software platform for the early care and education (ECE) system. It gives state agencies, cities and counties, child care resource and referral organizations (CCR&Rs), nonprofits, and school districts one system to run Pre-K program administration, family navigation, coordinated eligibility and enrollment, centralized eligibility screening, licensing, workforce development, quality management (QRIS), grants management, subsidy administration, tri-share administration, and program assurance. The platform is used by 500,000+ families, 50,000+ providers, and 500+ counties. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, BridgeCare is backed by Techstars and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. BridgeCare operates an API host but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer documentation, so this profile is identity-only.

companies.name: Daybreak
companies.description: Daybreak Health is a B2B mental health company that delivers teletherapy and mental health programs for K-12 students (ages 5-19) in partnership with school districts and health plans. Its services include one-on-one teletherapy, in-person and hybrid onsite programs, universal mental health screeners, and mental health classes, with programs tailored for BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and low-income student populations. Daybreak is a care-delivery organization sold to schools and payers rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Experiment
companies.description: Experiment is an online crowdfunding platform for scientific research that connects scientists directly with backers who fund individual studies. Researchers across biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, computer science, paleontology, economics, engineering, and neuroscience post projects with goals and budgets; the public pledges funds, follows lab notes, and shares in the discoveries. Experiment (formerly Microryza) also supports university institutions and dedicated funding programs, and publishes results and updates back to funders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, slow-ventures, and y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a live consumer website but no public developer API, docs, or well-known surface.

companies.name: Future
companies.description: Future (Future Research, Inc., future.co) is a consumer fitness technology company that delivers custom, one-on-one personal training through a mobile app. Members are paired with a dedicated certified coach who builds an individualized workout program, provides real-time messaging and accountability check-ins, and adapts the plan over time. The product includes an exercise library with form-guidance videos, flexible scheduling, and Apple Watch integration for workout tracking. Future is a direct-to-consumer subscription service (first month $50, then $199/month with a 30-day money-back guarantee) and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company.

companies.name: Ideal Invest
companies.description: Ideal Invest (operating as Pravaler) is a Brazilian fintech founded in 2002 and headquartered in Sao Paulo that provides private student financing for higher education. Through its Pravaler platform, students can split tuition payments across roughly twice the duration of a course, with a 100% digital, low-bureaucracy application, competitive monthly interest rates, and no ENEM requirement. Pravaler works with a network of 500+ partner higher-education institutions and has financed more than 400,000 students, channeling over R$12 billion into Brazilian education. The company is backed by Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Pravaler exposes a consumer web platform (simulation, application, digital signature) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or partner integration surface.

companies.name: Zogo Finance
companies.description: Zogo Finance is a gamified financial education platform (founded 2018, a Techstars portfolio company) that helps banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions engage and educate their customers. Its library of 1,200+ bite-sized financial literacy modules is delivered to end users through an embeddable, white-label SDK that partners drop into their existing digital banking apps and websites, plus a standalone mobile app and desktop web experience. Users earn redeemable points for completing lessons. Zogo is a B2B/enterprise offering distributed via SDK embed and mobile-banking integrations (Q2, NCR, Jack Henry Banno) rather than a public developer API; as of this pass no public API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

companies.name: 80,000 Hours
companies.description: 80,000 Hours is an independent nonprofit, founded in 2011 by Benjamin Todd and William MacAskill out of Oxford, that provides free research and support to help people use their careers to help solve the world's most pressing problems. The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours a typical person works over their lifetime. It publishes an evidence-based career guide, in-depth problem profiles, a long-form podcast, and one-on-one advising, and runs a curated high-impact job board at jobs.80000hours.org. Since 2016 it has ranked helping navigate the transition to advanced AI as its top priority. It is a content and career-advice organization rather than an API producer; no public developer API is published, though it does serve a machine-readable llms.txt index of its content.

companies.name: Admittedly
companies.description: myOptions (myoptions.org redirects to encourageme.com; operated as the Encourage platform by Encoura, LLC) is a free college and career planning platform for middle- and high-school students, families, and educators across the United States. Students explore colleges, majors, careers, and scholarships and get matched to institutions, while educators deliver guidance through lesson plans, preference forms, and reporting dashboards. The platform reports serving roughly 4 million students across 5,000 school districts and 10,000+ high schools in all 50 states and D.C., funded through partnerships with colleges and education providers rather than user fees. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation surface, and no real /.well-known/ documents (all such paths return the SPA/404 catch-all). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead under the stub slug 'admittedly'.

companies.name: AOne
companies.description: AOne is a Malaysia-based learning-centre management software company (operating publicly as AOneSchools) whose all-in-one platform is used by 4,000+ tuition centres, preschools, enrichment centres, sports academies, and language centres to automate billing, LHDN e-invoicing, attendance tracking, student and class management, and parent communication across connected web and mobile apps. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. The company's public surface today is a marketing website (aone.com.my) and a customer login/app at app.aoneschools.com; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface is currently published.

companies.name: Aprende
companies.description: Aprende (Aprende Institute) is an online vocational education platform delivering Spanish-language courses and diplomados to Hispanic entrepreneurs and professionals across the United States and Latin America. The platform offers on-demand, mobile-friendly training across six main areas — gastronomy, entrepreneurship, wellness, beauty, skilled trades, and hospitality/events — taught by expert instructors, and is backed by 500 Global. It operates as a consumer education company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and web properties in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Corca
companies.description: Corca is an AI-native, collaborative workspace for mathematics — a browser-based editor that lets people write math naturally (without special syntax), run calculations in real time, and collaborate the way teams do in Figma or Google Docs. Typing keywords like "sum" or "integral" surfaces the right symbols and functions, documents import from and export to LaTeX, and built-in AI helps solve problems, manipulate expressions, and generate code without switching tools. It is used for lab research, lecture creation, team knowledge bases, and publishing academic work. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Corca raised a $7.8M round (led by NEA, with Bloomberg Beta, NVIDIA's NVentures, Daft Capital, Slow Ventures, Liquid 2, Path Ventures, and Mana Ventures). The product is a consumer/team SaaS application; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profile.

companies.name: Emeritus
companies.description: Emeritus is a global online education company that partners with more than 80 premier universities — including Wharton, MIT, Columbia, Harvard, Kellogg, and UC Berkeley — to deliver outcome-based executive education, professional certificates, and skill-development programs to over 500,000 learners worldwide. It operates across individual learners, enterprise/corporate training, and university-branded partnership programs, spanning topics such as AI and machine learning, data science, finance, leadership, and digital transformation through instructor-led online and blended formats. Emeritus is backed by Accel and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Emeritus publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Emma
companies.description: Emma (by EDAILABS) is an AI-powered English language learning application built around a 3D interactive avatar tutor that offers real-time spoken conversation practice, instant pronunciation and grammar corrections, and personalized, adaptive learning paths. Positioned as "more than just a chatbot," the app models native accents and speech patterns for judgment-free practice available 24/7, and reports more than 500,000 users. It is a consumer iOS mobile application backed by Seedcamp; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

companies.name: Freckle Education
companies.description: Freckle is an adaptive learning platform from Renaissance that delivers differentiated, standards-aligned math and English Language Arts (ELA) practice for K-12 students. Teachers assign work and monitor progress while students practice at their own level, with the platform adapting question difficulty to each learner across 70,000+ math questions and 1,000+ ELA passages. Administrators manage rosters and dashboards at the school and district level. Freckle is a school- and classroom-facing application acquired by Renaissance Learning; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Incluyeme
companies.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities. Its online platform connects candidates with disabilities to inclusive employers, offering job listings, virtual training courses, scholarships, and mentorship for individuals, alongside inclusive-hiring consulting, talent sourcing, staff training, and physical/web accessibility evaluation for companies. Operating across roughly a dozen countries in Latin America (Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, Paraguay and more), it has registered hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities and placed thousands into roles with 100+ corporate clients. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Kibin
companies.description: Kibin is a consumer study and academic-writing company operating at kibin.com, trusted by students since 2011. Its newest product is an AI-powered study partner (iOS app) that turns lectures, notes, PDFs, and YouTube videos into personalized study guides, quizzes, flashcards, transcripts, and explanations to help students learn faster and build mastery. Alongside the study app, Kibin also runs its long-standing academic-writing surface — professional essay editing, a paper grader, a thesis-statement generator, essay examples, and a writing blog. Kibin is a B2C, mobile- and web-delivered product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

companies.name: LabLabee
companies.description: LabLabee is an AI-powered enablement, testing and troubleshooting platform for telecom teams, positioning itself as "the Copilot for Telco Engineers." The platform delivers on-demand, hands-on labs, sandboxes, learning paths and skill tests covering 4G/5G and Open RAN, IMS, network OAM, SDN and IP networking, telco cloud (OpenStack, OpenShift, Kubernetes, Docker), DevOps and GitOps automation (Terraform, Ansible, CI/CD), Linux, IAM and cybersecurity, and Industry 4.0 and IoT. Three AI capabilities sit on top of the lab catalog: AI Ask (search across telecom standards, vendor documentation and enterprise knowledge), AI Test (automated test execution and configuration validation) and AI Troubleshoot (automated trace analysis and root-cause identification). LabLabee serves telcos, universities, system integrators, network vendors and industrial private-network operators. Founded by Samir Tahraoui (CEO) and Mahfoud S. A. Mebarek (CPO), the company is backed by Accel, Kima Ventures, Reach Capital, Brighteye Ventures and 500 Global, and has been recognized as Best Telecom Startup by the World Communication Awards and with the TM Forum Growth Challenge Award. As of this enrichment pass LabLabee publishes no public developer program - no API documentation, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, CLI or public package artifacts were found on any of its surfaces.

companies.name: Linguatrip
companies.description: Linguatrip is a language-education and language-travel company founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global. It operates two connected businesses: a booking marketplace for accredited language schools abroad — covering course selection, accommodation, airport transfers and visa support across countries including the United Kingdom, Malta and the United Arab Emirates — and its own online English school offering 25+ self-paced courses, one-to-one tutoring, speaking clubs and exam preparation for IELTS, TOEFL, GMAT, GRE and SAT. It also provides higher-education placement consulting for US, UK and Canadian universities. Linguatrip publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; its surfaces are consumer web properties in four languages with pricing in 18 currencies.

companies.name: Manara
companies.description: Manara is an upskilling and professional development platform focused on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, specializing in training for emerging technologies including AI and cloud computing. It runs enterprise workforce-development programs, national government training initiatives, and individual learning and certification courses, connecting a community of MENA software engineers and technologists with global career opportunities. The company reports 300,000+ learners trained, 2,500+ certifications awarded, operations across 40+ countries, and 500+ job placements. Manara publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Marcopolo Learning
companies.description: MarcoPolo Learning is an award-winning early childhood education technology company, founded in 2013, that builds premium video content, instructional support, and learning apps for preschool and kindergarten. Its products include MarcoPolo For Educators (curriculum-aligned classroom video and educator guides), MarcoPolo For Families (Emmy-nominated videos plus literacy and math games), MarcoPolo World School (kindergarten readiness), MarcoPolo Professional Development for teachers, and The Polos animated series. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MarcoPolo Learning publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable developer surface; it is a consumer/educator app business, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Mind Candy, Moshi
companies.description: Mind Candy Ltd is a London-based children's media and technology company, originally known for the Moshi Monsters online game and now operating Moshi, an award-winning children's app for sleep, relaxation and learning. Moshi offers hundreds of hours of bedtime stories, sleep sounds, music, white noise and educational activities delivered through iOS and Android consumer apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Moshi is a direct-to-consumer subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Mision Admision
companies.description: Misión Admisión is a Mexican education-technology company based in Mérida that prepares high school and university applicants for standardized admission exams such as EXANI I, EXANI II, PAA, and the UNAM, IPN, and UAM entrance tests. Its consumer web platform (misionadmision.com) delivers self-paced online courses, video lessons, interactive study capsules, thousands of practice questions, full-length exam simulators, live virtual and in-person classes, and the physical Sputnik smartbook guides. Founded in 2001 and online since 2015, the company is a seed-stage portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing EdTech platform and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

companies.name: Mujer Financiera
companies.description: Mujer Financiera is a Latin American financial-education platform founded in 2018 in Buenos Aires, Argentina by Sabrina Castelli, focused on closing the gender gap in financial inclusion. It delivers courses, packs, and multi-month programs (MF Platinum) on budgeting, saving, and investing, alongside a mobile app for tracking personal finances, a supportive community, a newsletter, and corporate financial-education services for companies. The platform reports hundreds of thousands of women served across 12+ countries and is backed by 500 Global. It is a business-to-consumer fintech/edtech offering and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Novel Effect
companies.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Numerade
companies.description: Numerade is an education technology company that helps students learn STEM subjects through short, expert-created video solutions, step-by-step textbook explanations, and an AI study tutor branded as Ace. Ace responds to typed questions, uploaded notes, quizzes, and worksheets, and can summarize material to help students prepare for exams. The platform spans math, science, and other STEM courses with a large library of instructor-led problem walkthroughs and practice questions. Numerade is a venture-backed consumer learning product and does not currently expose a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of General Catalyst and enriched by probing the public site (2026-07-20).

companies.name: Photomath
companies.description: Photomath is a mobile math-learning application that lets students scan a printed or handwritten math problem with their phone camera and returns step-by-step explanations, custom visual aids, and animated solving methods across topics from elementary arithmetic through calculus. Originally built by Croatian computer-vision company Microblink and later spun out as an independent education company backed by Menlo Ventures and Goldman Sachs, Photomath was acquired by Google in 2023 and now operates within Google (support is handled through Google's Help Center). It is a consumer subscription product distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. The company previously stated it would not release a public Photomath SDK. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched to capture the company's public web and domain-security surface; no first-party API surface exists to catalog.

companies.name: Praktika.ai Company
companies.description: Praktika.ai is an AI-powered language-learning application that lets learners have spoken conversations with lifelike AI avatar tutors and receive instant feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary. The product spans mobile (iOS and Android) and web, with personalized study plans and speaking, listening, reading, and writing exercises across many languages, plus a B2B offering for organizations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Praktika publishes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation were found — so this profile captures the company identity and web properties rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Prodigy Finance
companies.description: Prodigy Finance is an education-finance provider offering postgraduate (master's degree) loans to international students, funding applicants from 120+ countries who study at business schools and universities worldwide. Using a borderless credit model that assesses future earning potential rather than requiring collateral or a local co-signer, the company has funded over 47,000 international master's students across 18+ years. It operates consumer-facing web applications for loan application, account management, and disbursement, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

companies.name: SplashLearn
companies.description: SplashLearn (operated by StudyPad, Inc.) is a game-based learning platform offering math and English/ELA curriculum for preschool through Grade 5 students, used by parents, teachers, schools, and homeschoolers. It delivers interactive games, worksheets, lesson plans, and progress tracking across web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps, plus homeschool, summer-learning, and SpringBoard programs. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web/security surface.

companies.name: The Learning Experience
companies.description: The Learning Experience is an early childhood education and childcare franchise operating academies of early education for children from six weeks to six years old across a nationwide network of centers. Its programs span infant, toddler, preschool, and pre-kindergarten care built on a proprietary curriculum. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-facing childcare operator it publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture.

companies.name: Think Parametric
companies.description: Think Parametric is an online learning platform for architecture, engineering, and design professionals, offering expert-led courses and professional certifications in computational and parametric design tools including Rhino, Grasshopper, Revit, Dynamo, SketchUp, and V-Ray. Membership plans give individuals and organizations access to a library of 60+ courses taught by practitioners from leading firms such as SOM, BIG, Gensler, AECOM, and Arup, alongside community forums, downloadable assets, and progress tracking. Backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Upkid
companies.description: Upkid is a childcare staffing marketplace that connects early childhood programs such as daycares and preschools with qualified, pre-vetted substitute and full-time teachers. Programs post shifts and roles while educators find flexible teaching opportunities through the Upkid web and mobile apps, with an ATS-style Hiring Hub for full-time childcare hiring. Upkid operates across metro areas in Georgia, Utah, and Arizona and is a Techstars portfolio company. Upkid publishes no public API or developer portal; its web app is a client of a Firebase backend.

companies.name: Wukong Education
companies.description: WuKong Education is an online education company headquartered in Auckland, New Zealand that delivers live online classes in Chinese language, math, and English ELA for kids, taught by certified teachers to students across more than 100 countries and regions. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, it is a consumer edtech business with a student classroom portal but no public developer portal or documented APIs.

companies.name: QuEra Computing
companies.description: QuEra Computing is a Boston-area neutral-atom quantum computing company, founded in 2021 by scientists from Harvard and MIT. Its flagship system, Aquila, is a 256-qubit field-programmable analog neutral-atom quantum processor that has been publicly available since November 2022 through Amazon Braket and through a direct Premium Access channel. QuEra develops Bloqade, an open-source software stack for neutral-atom quantum computing delivered as a Python SDK (Bloqade Python) and as the original Bloqade.jl Julia package, along with surrounding tooling for circuits, analog control, atom shuttling, decoders, and tensor-network simulation. The company is building toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with its Gemini-class next-generation systems and has demonstrated logical-level magic state distillation on neutral-atom hardware. QuEra works with HPC centers, national labs (NERSC, Los Alamos), DARPA, NEDO/AIST, NVIDIA, AWS, BCG X, Deloitte, Classiq, Kipu Quantum, Wolfram Research, and enterprise customers including BP, BASF, Merck, and Amgen. The system is consumed via the Bloqade SDK or AWS Braket; QuEra does not currently expose a public REST API to its QPU.

companies.name: Praxis Labs
companies.description: Praxis Labs is an AI-powered leadership and human-skills learning platform, surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and acquired by Torch. Its flagship product, Pivotal Practice, uses immersive simulations, personalized AI coaching, and role-play scenarios to build critical management capabilities such as difficult conversations and performance discussions, with behavior-change tracking and ROI analytics. The learning application runs at practice.praxislabs.co behind login and integrates with HR/L&D systems including Workday, Docebo, and Degreed. Praxis Labs is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. No public API, developer portal, or SDK was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile rather than an API provider.

companies.name: Community Labs
companies.description: Community Labs is an independent research organization founded in 2022 by Tate Berenbaum, oriented toward a single belief: access to the future of intelligence should not be gate kept by the hardware people can afford. The company raised a $30M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, originally operating as a native software development company and venture studio accelerating developer tools and adoption of the Arweave permaweb, and has since refocused on local and consumer-hardware AI inference research. Its open source surface spans Hypura, a storage-tier-aware LLM inference scheduler for Apple Silicon that exposes an Ollama-compatible HTTP API, Autolab, an autonomous research orchestration framework, and the labscommunity GitHub organization of Arweave developer libraries including ArweaveKit, Arweave Wallet Kit, and the Arweave Storage SDK.

companies.name: Bloomy
companies.description: Bloomy (bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered adaptive learning platform for K-12 students, founded by Alex Southmayd and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). The product diagnoses each student's knowledge gaps, builds a personalized standards-aligned learning path across English Language Arts, Math, and Writing, and delivers Socratic AI tutoring plus mastery-based practice, requiring 90%+ mastery before a student advances. It integrates third-party diagnostic/assessment data (i-Ready, NWEA MAP) and provides a real-time teacher dashboard. Bloomy serves traditional districts, charter schools, homeschools, and microschools, and sells to families via monthly or annual subscriptions (with ESA/EFA fund eligibility in some states). As of this profile Bloomy publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this record captures its verified public identity and legal/account surface only.

companies.name: Brit + Co
companies.description: Brit + Co is a lifestyle and entertainment media platform founded by Brit Morin that publishes content and creative education for a primarily women audience. It covers self-care, food, home and DIY, travel, relationships, celebrity and entertainment news, horoscopes, shopping guides, and games, and operates a learning platform (learn.brit.co) offering more than one hundred creative online classes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures. It is a consumer media and e-learning brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Draxon
companies.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Education Holdings 1 (The Princeton Review)
companies.description: Education Holdings 1 operates The Princeton Review, an educational services company offering standardized test preparation, one-on-one and on-demand tutoring, and college, graduate, medical, and law school admissions counseling. The Princeton Review prepares students for the SAT, ACT, PSAT, AP, MCAT, DAT, OAT, LSAT, GRE, GMAT, SSAT, ISEE, and SHSAT through live, self-paced, and honors courses, publishes college and graduate school rankings and guidebooks, and provides free practice tests, events, and study resources. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. The Princeton Review operates a consumer web presence rather than a public developer program; it publishes an llms.txt AI-discovery file but does not expose a documented public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: Ello
companies.description: Ello is a public-benefit AI education company building a 1:1 AI reading and math tutor for children ages 4-9. Its consumer app pairs proprietary child-speech recognition (trained on 100K+ hours of kids' audio) with generative AI and adaptive teaching agents to deliver personalized, sub-second, voice-based reading instruction grounded in the Science of Reading, plus a large catalog of leveled e-books, a "Storytime" create-your-own story feature, and parent progress reports. Recognized as one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2024 and backed by Y Combinator, Goodwater, Project A, and Homebrew, Ello is a consumer (B2C) product with no public developer API program at this time.

companies.name: Kartable
companies.description: Kartable is a French online education platform (edtech) delivering standards-aligned learning for students from primary through secondary school (CE1 to Terminale, ages 6-18). It provides more than 1,000 course summaries, thousands of corrected exercises, and quizzes across 16 subjects including mathematics, French, history, physics, and languages, authored by teachers from the French Education Ministry. Its "Alfa" AI tutor answers questions 24/7, generates custom quizzes from photos of coursework, and guides students through homework, while parents follow progress from a dedicated dashboard. Kartable is a consumer subscription product (from EUR 7.99/month) and does not publish a public developer API. Backed by Partech.

companies.name: Leland
companies.description: Leland is a marketplace for ambitious people to access the coaching, classes, and community they need to reach career and educational goals. It connects individuals with vetted 1-on-1 coaches across MBA and college admissions, management consulting, investment banking, private equity, product management, law, medicine, and executive and career development, and sells structured live programs, bootcamps, and test prep for the GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MCAT, SAT, and ACT. Leland+ is a subscription content library of video guides, essay and resume examples, templates, and expert-built AI tools. For organizations Leland offers AI-native talent training, agentic workflow deployment, recruiting, and outplacement, plus university and HR partnerships. Leland publishes no public API or developer portal as of 2026-07-19.

companies.name: Lendorse
companies.description: Lendorse GmbH is a Berlin-based education-finance company that funds international master's students studying in Europe through Income Share Agreements (ISAs) instead of traditional credit-scored loans. Students receive between EUR 3,000 and EUR 20,000 toward tuition, visa deposits, relocation and living costs, then repay a fixed 6-12% share of gross monthly income for 12 to 60 months once they earn above a EUR 2,500 monthly salary floor, with total repayment capped at 2.3x the funded amount. No collateral, co-signer, parental guarantor or credit check is required, which opens funding to students from developing and emerging markets who are normally excluded. Lendorse also provides mentorship, CV review, mock interviews and industry introductions. It covers universities in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland, went through the Techstars and ABN AMRO Future of Finance Accelerator, and raised EUR 1.75M co-led by LUMO Labs and Soulmates Ventures. Lendorse publishes no public API, SDKs or developer portal as of July 2026; this profile is a company record rather than an API profile.

companies.name: On Deck
companies.description: On Deck (now operating as the On Deck Founder Fellowship, ODF) is a founder fellowship and startup community program that helps aspiring entrepreneurs start companies through an intense, in-person cohort experience focused on meeting co-founders, exploring ideas, and gaining conviction. Backed by Canaan Partners, On Deck provides mentorship, a peer community, and startup perks. It is a program and community platform rather than a developer or API product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

companies.name: Quizlet
companies.description: Quizlet is a San Francisco-based global learning platform offering flashcards, practice tests, and AI-powered study tools used by students, teachers, and lifelong learners. Core features include user-created and expert-verified study sets, Learn mode (adaptive practice), Test mode, Match game, Spaced Repetition, and an AI tutor (Q-Chat / Magic Notes) that generates flashcards, summaries, practice questions, and explanations from uploaded notes, PDFs, slides, and textbooks. Quizlet Plus is the company's consumer subscription, and Quizlet for Schools / Teachers provides licensed offerings for classrooms. The platform integrates with Google Classroom (share-as-assignment) and Canvas (embeddable widgets) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK — the legacy Developer API 2.0 (`quizlet.com/api/2.0`) was effectively wound down to partners-only and is not openly registrable. Quizlet's GitHub organization (`github.com/quizlet`) hosts internal tooling, GitHub Actions, and forks of OSS dependencies (HHVM/Hack, PHPUnit, Mockery, Stylus, etc.) rather than a developer-facing API platform.

companies.name: Sidechat
companies.description: Sidechat is an anonymous, campus-based social networking app for college students, built by Flower Ave Inc in New York City and backed by Canaan Partners. Students verify with a school email to join their college's private, location- and campus-scoped community where they post text, images, and polls, vote, and chat anonymously in a Reddit-like feed. Sidechat launched in early 2022, acquired Yik Yak in 2023, and operates primarily as an iOS consumer app. It publishes no official public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures the company's public web presence and identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is a consumer-first interactive STEM learning platform that delivers bite-sized, problem-solving-driven courses in math, computer science, data science, and science to over 10 million learners on web, iOS, and Android. Brilliant for Educators offers free Premium access to K-12 teachers and students, with Google Classroom roster sync, COPPA/FERPA/GDPR compliance, and a teacher portal for class management. Brilliant does not publish a public developer API or partner SDK — the product is consumer- and classroom-facing, and integration with school ecosystems is limited to Google Classroom roster sync.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is an online learning platform for interactive STEM education, covering mathematics, computer science, data, and science. Headquartered in San Francisco and used by over ten million learners worldwide, Brilliant pairs guided, problem-first lessons with adaptive practice that blends classic intelligent tutoring systems, machine-learning recommender systems, and natural-language conversations. The platform is delivered through brilliant.org and native iOS and Android apps, with a freemium model and a Brilliant Premium subscription that unlocks the full course catalog, including expanding AI-powered features such as personalized tutoring conversations and on-the-fly generation of interactive content. Brilliant operates as a direct-to-consumer subscription business with an educator program for classroom access; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program, and the `github.com/brilliant` org on GitHub is an unrelated namespace of personal projects rather than an official Brilliant presence.

companies.name: Citruslabs
companies.description: Citruslabs is a clinical research organization (CRO) that designs and runs clinical trials, consumer perception studies, and randomized controlled trials for consumer health brands across supplements, skincare, pet health, food and beverage, longevity, and women's health. It handles IRB approval, protocol design, participant recruitment, decentralized data collection, and statistical analysis, then turns results into regulator-reviewed, marketing-ready product claims for retailers, advertising, and packaging. Studies range from DIY consumer perception studies to full randomized controlled trials, typically completing in four to sixteen weeks.

companies.name: Goodfellow
companies.description: Goodfellow (Goodfellow Advanced Materials) is a global specialty-materials supplier founded in 1946 and headquartered in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, serving research, prototyping and specialized manufacturing markets in more than 111 countries. Its catalog spans over 70,000 stocked products drawn from 700+ different materials in many forms, including metals, alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites, compounds and glass, alongside custom fabrication and laboratory testing services. Customers include universities, government research facilities, laboratories and advanced manufacturers, served through subsidiaries in the United States, China, France and Germany. Goodfellow was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2021 to help digitize its operations and fund materials acquisitions. Goodfellow is a business-to-business e-commerce and catalog operation; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks.

companies.name: Hyperpad
companies.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

companies.name: IXL Learning
companies.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

companies.name: Kyros College Prep
companies.description: Kyros (kyros.ai) is an AI-driven college preparation and admissions platform. In the company's own words, it is "a College Prep Platform by former Googlers, Admissions Officers, and Professors" that "uses AI to offer 100K+ summer and financial aid programs." The product combines student assessments for college and major fit, one-on-one counseling, college essay and letter-of-recommendation support, extracurricular and summer-program discovery, and structured program tracks such as Future You Lab, the UC Bootcamp, and industry immersion and research programs. Kyros also sells through partner channels, with education-partner, VAR, counselor-advisory, college-success, and Fortune 1000 employer offerings, and publishes a large admissions blog. As of 2026-07-19 Kyros publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API description.

companies.name: Unitree Robotics
companies.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

companies.name: Zoog
companies.description: Zoog is a consumer mobile app platform that lets families create and share personalized video books and songs for children. Users read classic kids' stories or sing popular kids' songs while the app adds filters, effects, and music to produce custom animated videos that connect loved ones across distances. Founded in 2021 by Yoav Oren and Matan Guttman and backed by Techstars, Zoog is used by families worldwide. It is a consumer product with no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Cajal Technologies
companies.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

companies.name: Lagou
companies.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Cartwheel Care
companies.description: Cartwheel (Cartwheel Care) is a school-based youth mental health provider that partners with K-12 school districts to deliver rapid-access, evidence-based therapy and psychiatric care to students. Through licensed clinicians it offers individual and group therapy, medication management, and parent guidance, with Care Coordinators contacting families within 24 hours of a school referral and initial appointments typically available within 7-10 days; a course of care generally lasts two to six months. The company is backed by General Catalyst and operates across 25+ school districts in multiple states. Cartwheel publishes no public API or developer surface; its software footprint is a school- and family-facing web application at app.cartwheel.org, hosted on the HIPAA-compliant Aptible platform.

companies.name: EdSights
companies.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

companies.name: Udacity
companies.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

companies.name: Kilsar
companies.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: University Startups
companies.description: University Startups is an AI-powered transition planning management platform built for special education teams. The platform helps teachers create IDEA-compliant IEP transition plans in under 10 minutes, audits plans against 11 IDEA Indicator 13 criteria in under 90 seconds, generates SMART-format IEP goals, and engages students with disabilities in building their own transition plans, alongside a college and career readiness curriculum and internship simulator. A Techstars portfolio company serving United States school districts including NYC Public Schools; no public developer API surface is published.

companies.name: Atypical AI
companies.description: Atypical AI is an artificial-intelligence and learning-science lab building generative-AI learning products for educators, learners, and content creators. Its flagship product, ExamJam, is an AI tutor that pairs adaptive, personalized tutoring with trusted exam content from major publishers (Pearson, McGraw Hill, Collins) to help students prepare for and revise toward their exams. Founded in 2023 and based in San Francisco, the woman-owned company builds personalized tutoring, exam preparation, content creation, collaboration, and student-success measurement tools grounded in learning science. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta; it publishes a consumer product surface (web + mobile) and no public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Brite
companies.description: Brite is a white-label learning management system (LMS) platform for STEM education, giving educators, academies, and learning centers a single operational tool to run computer-science programs in game and web development. It bundles a ready-made curriculum, classroom and roster management, student progress reporting, and teacher accounts, replacing spreadsheets and disparate software with one branded platform. Brite is offered on free, per-student Professional, and custom school/district tiers. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Dreambound
companies.description: Dreambound is a career and technical education marketplace that helps job seekers discover, compare, and enroll in vocational training programs across healthcare, technology, business, and the skilled trades. The platform aggregates thousands of schools and hundreds of programs, letting students filter by location, schedule, format (online, hybrid, or in person), and price, with enrollment coaches guiding them into certifications such as certified nursing assistant, medical billing, phlebotomy, and sterile processing. The service is free for students and monetizes through schools and workforce partners who list and advertise their programs. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Collaborative Fund, and 8VC, Dreambound is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Englease Technologies SPV Ltd
companies.description: Englease is an online English language learning platform serving students across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, founded by Omar Shihan and headquartered in Dubai Internet City, UAE. The platform blends live classes running 16 hours a day across all seven days, self-paced on-demand courses, pronunciation and practice tools, and conversation clubs, with proficiency-based learning paths from beginner to advanced and UK-accredited certifications. Englease serves individuals, corporations, schools, and specific industries including hospitality, call centers, retail, banking, and healthcare. Englease Technologies SPV Ltd is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking. The consumer product is delivered through a web/app experience; no public developer API surface has been identified.

companies.name: FundMiner
companies.description: FundMiner is a fund management and donor stewardship platform for mission-driven organizations, giving universities, healthcare systems, and community foundations one place to manage the full fund lifecycle. It combines fund management with compliance monitoring, impact and donor reporting, and a branded donor portal that gives donors real-time visibility into how their gifts are used. The platform integrates with existing financial systems and offers role-based dashboards and access controls. FundMiner is a Techstars-backed company; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API reference at this time, so this profile captures its public identity and web presence.

companies.name: Guild
companies.description: Guild (formerly Guild Education) is an education benefits and career opportunity platform that partners with large employers to fund and administer workforce education, upskilling, and career-mobility programs for their frontline and hourly employees. Employers offer Guild as a benefit; employees access a curated marketplace of degrees, certificates, bootcamps, English-language, and professional-skilling programs from vetted learning providers, plus coaching and career navigation to move into higher-demand roles.
