Guild is a B2B/B2B2C SaaS platform sold to enterprise HR and talent-development teams to fill critical roles, improve retention, increase internal mobility, and prove measurable ROI. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado, Guild is a venture-backed company. This profile was surfaced from investor portfolios and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Guild publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

companies.name: Mentor Spaces
companies.description: Mentor Spaces is a structured mentorship platform that helps nonprofits, universities, and companies launch, manage, and measure mentorship programs at scale. The software handles automated mentor-mentee matching, scheduling, communication, and real-time outcome tracking so organizations can secure and renew grant funding with funder-ready impact reports, improve student persistence and career outcomes, engage alumni in time-bound structured mentorship, and run skills-based volunteering and corporate CSR/ESG programs. A public developer API and custom integrations are offered only on the enterprise Thrive tier (with SSO); no public API documentation is published. Founded by Chris Motley and backed by Techstars.

companies.name: One Month
companies.description: One Month is an online coding education platform that teaches beginners practical software and web development skills through short, project-based video courses designed to be completed in about a month. Its catalog spans programming languages and frameworks such as Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, HTML & CSS, SQL, and WordPress, alongside professional skills like project management, using a "watch, do, repeat" methodology of hands-on lessons and follow-along projects. One Month markets itself to career changers and non-programmers looking to accelerate into technical roles, and publishes a supporting blog of programming tutorials and career guidance. It is a consumer-facing learning product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: OnMyGrad
companies.description: OnMyGrad is a Hong Kong-based campus-recruitment and career-learning SaaS platform that helps employers connect with university talent across Southeast Asia through virtual job-tasting and work-experience programs. Founded in 2021 by Jesse Chow and Chun Hin Anthony So, its B2B2C "OnMyGrad Space" lets employers build branded profiles, run virtual talent pipelines, and evaluate candidates, while students access immersive career and industry learning content from leading employers. The company launched its MVP in February 2021, raised pre-seed funding from 500 Global, and is expanding into Singapore and Taiwan. It operates a public marketing site and a web application but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Pandai
companies.description: Pandai is a Malaysian education technology company founded in 2020 that operates a digital learning platform for primary and secondary school students. The app aligns to Malaysia's national curriculum (DSKP) across KSSR Years 1-6 and KSSM Forms 1-5, including SPM exam preparation, and helps learners improve their grades through interactive quizzes, tests, exams, topical practice, notes, flashcards, videos, and live tutoring. Features include personalized assessments, an AI-powered revision assistant (Ask Pbot), gamified learning with battles, leaderboards and rewards, and performance tracking via scorecards and report cards. Pandai is a consumer-facing learning app and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Prisms VR
companies.description: Prisms VR (Prisms) is an educational technology company building what it calls the world's first spatial learning platform, where students learn core math, science, and other subjects by abstracting up from immersive, first-person physical experiences delivered in virtual reality. Founded by MIT engineer-turned-educator Anurupa Ganguly, the teacher-facing platform uses kinesthetic, embodied learning to help students grasp abstract concepts and aims to develop curious, resilient thinkers. Prisms is an a16z portfolio company; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and profiled through the enrichment pipeline. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

companies.name: Skool
companies.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

companies.name: Zzish
companies.description: Zzish is an EdTech company (a Techstars-backed startup) building a K-12 learning product suite used by teachers and students across 180 countries. Its flagship product, Quizalize, is a classroom quiz and formative-assessment platform; the portfolio also includes Blockerzz (a 3D game engine with quiz games and coding tutorials), Marvely.ai (AI-powered, exam-aligned language tutoring), Quizalize Insights (leadership dashboards for tracking academic progress), and QUAT (a customer-analytics platform for schools and EdTech partners). Zzish reports 250k+ teachers onboarded in the last two years and 250m+ questions answered since launch. As of this enrichment pass, Zzish publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer-documentation surface.

companies.name: Avarra
companies.description: Avarra is an AI-powered sales training and enablement platform that helps revenue teams onboard, coach, and certify sales representatives at scale. The platform turns real sales conversations into AI-driven role-play simulations, delivers personalized coaching feedback, standardizes sales methodology across teams and regions, and reports certification and performance analytics. Its workflow moves through five stages: Capture, Train, Practice, Certify, and Performance Insights, with the stated goal of cutting new-hire ramp time in half. Avarra is a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company. As of this profile Avarra publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Modular Robotics
companies.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

companies.name: Nurture
companies.description: Nurture is an EdTech company that turns children's screen time into skill-building experiences through an interactive storytelling app for kids aged 5-7. Built on the thesis that AI is mastering information while human skills — critical thinking, curiosity, empathy, creativity, and resilience — still need to be nurtured, the app delivers character-driven story adventures with practice-based learning, no in-app purchases, no ads, and no endless autoplay. It is COPPA-compliant and features licensed brands such as Care Bears, Crayola, and Pocoyo. Nurture is a consumer mobile product distributed on the iOS App Store, Google Play, and Amazon Appstore, sold as a $36/year subscription with a 7-day free trial. It is a Seedcamp portfolio company. As a consumer application, Nurture publishes no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface; api.nurture.is serves only an internal app backend.

companies.name: Brightwheel
companies.description: Brightwheel (mybrightwheel.com) is an all-in-one childcare and early education management platform used by childcare centers, preschools, and early-learning programs to run daily operations - attendance and check-in, digital daily sheets, tuition billing and payments, enrollment and admissions, staff/timecards, classroom (room) management, learning assessments, and real-time parent messaging and photo/video sharing. As of this catalog entry, Brightwheel does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key signup, OpenAPI specification, or webhook documentation. The only Brightwheel API activity that is publicly acknowledged is bespoke, contract-scoped work built for individual government partners - for example a private API implemented to submit attendance and subsidy data to Iowa's childcare subsidy data system - and inbound integrations where Brightwheel pushes data into third-party products (e.g. staff timecards to Gusto for payroll). None of these expose a documented API surface that outside developers can build against. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

companies.name: Codecademy
companies.description: Codecademy is a New York City–based online learning platform offering interactive coding tutorials, career paths, certifications, and bootcamps across programming languages, data science, AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and web development. Founded in 2011 by Zach Sims and Ryan Bubinski, the company built its reputation on browser-based interactive exercises that let learners write and execute code without local setup, and grew to serve millions of registered learners. Codecademy was acquired by Skillsoft in April 2022 for approximately 525 million dollars in a cash-and-stock deal, and now operates as the consumer- and individual- developer-facing brand within Skillsoft's broader corporate learning portfolio, complementing Skillsoft Percipio for enterprise customers. Codecademy's products include the free tier, Codecademy Plus, Codecademy Pro, career paths, skill paths, professional certifications, full cohort-based bootcamps (via Codecademy and Skillsoft's Global Knowledge arm), and a workspaces feature for project work. The company does not expose a public developer REST API, SDK, or partner API program for programmatic access to courses, progress, or learner data; its primary surface is the codecademy.com web application and mobile apps, with enterprise content delivery handled through Skillsoft channels.

companies.name: Prodigy Education
companies.description: Prodigy Education is a Canadian K-8 game-based learning company best known for Prodigy Math and Prodigy English — fantasy RPG-style products in which students battle and quest by answering curriculum-aligned questions. The product is free for teachers and is monetized through optional parent memberships. Prodigy is consumer- and classroom-facing with no public developer API or partner program. Its integration surface is school rostering and SSO: Clever (SSO + Secure Sync district rostering), ClassLink (SSO, with OneRoster district rostering rolling out), and Google (SSO + Google Classroom assignment creation).

companies.name: Chegg
companies.description: Chegg is an American education technology company that provides direct-to-student learning services, including 24/7 homework and expert Q&A help, step-by-step textbook solutions, practice questions, and writing, grammar, and citation tools. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Chegg began as a textbook-rental marketplace and expanded into a subscription study-support platform (Chegg Study, Chegg Writing, Chegg Math Solver) plus tutoring and skills offerings. Chegg operates as a consumer web/mobile product rather than a developer platform: it exposes no public developer portal, published API, or SDKs at this time. Its public technical surface is limited to a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program on HackerOne and standard web security/policy pages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Chief
companies.description: Chief is a private membership network built to connect and support senior women leaders, serving executives across more than 10,000 companies with roughly 44% of members in C-suite roles. Membership combines vetted peer Core Groups, one-on-one and group executive coaching, business training (including programming with partners such as The Wharton School), member Clubhouses, and ChiefX events, plus an enterprise offering for companies sponsoring their women leaders. Chief is a membership-and-community company rather than an API provider, so this profile is an identity record in the API Evangelist network with no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Cleverdeck
companies.description: CleverDeck is a spaced-repetition flashcard application for iOS, built by an independent developer to help people learn and retain vocabulary and other material more efficiently. It ships hand-made premium decks covering roughly the 3,000 most common words in major foreign languages — Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Russian and advanced English — with translations, transliterations, images, native-speaker audio, and example sentences in both English and the target language. The app uses the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm (as popularized by SuperMemo and Anki) with a customizable learning schedule, cross-device sync, and full offline support. It is free to create and study your own content, with unlimited access to the premium decks for $3 per month. CleverDeck is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or agent-facing surface.

companies.name: Fizz
companies.description: Fizz is a social platform built for college campuses, connecting students within their own school communities across 700+ campuses in the United States. Founded by Stanford students, Fizz gives verified students an anonymous, hyper-local feed to find their community and join the conversation, buy and sell through Fizz Marketplace, and engage under community values of being supportive, curious, honest, and brave. The platform is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and NEA. Fizz is a consumer mobile social app and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface for network discovery and monitoring.

companies.name: Piazza
companies.description: Piazza is an online question-and-answer platform for higher education that connects students, teaching assistants, and professors in a single wiki-style collaborative space for each class. Instructors run a Piazza for their course where students ask and answer questions, post anonymously, use a LaTeX and code editor for technical content, and receive instructor-endorsed answers. Piazza integrates with every major learning management system (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Sakai, Desire2Learn, and others) via the LTI standard for single-click class creation, roster-based automatic enrollment, and automatic single sign-on. It is used across thousands of universities in more than 90 countries and is FERPA-compliant. Piazza does not publish an official public developer API; LMS connectivity is delivered through LTI, and only community projects wrap its internal endpoints.

companies.name: HumanQ
companies.description: HumanQ is an execution-capability and intelligence platform that helps organizations move critical work forward through structured, live execution sprints called QPods. Each QPod is a 60-minute facilitated session, led by trained "Catalysts," for small groups of up to six participants working through decision drag, unclear ownership, and cross-team stalls. HumanQ is offered as HumanQ Scale (an enterprise-wide program with weekly and monthly tracks, on-demand drop-ins, and deep customization) and HumanQ Teams (a manager-led tool for up to four groups, live in two weeks with no contract). Progress is tracked through the QStart, QImpact, and QSignal measurement framework, with delivery across 74 countries. HumanQ is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. It is a managed-services platform and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

companies.name: Web3 Foundation
companies.description: Web3 Foundation is a Swiss nonprofit founded in 2017 by Gavin Wood that funds research and development teams building the foundation of a decentralized web (Web3). It stewards and supports the Polkadot and Kusama networks, operates a research hub and an education/wiki program, and historically ran the Web3 Foundation Grants Program (now discontinued) to seed open-source software and protocol research. It is a funding and research organization rather than a traditional API provider: it publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface, but does maintain an RFC 9116 security.txt and a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure program.

companies.name: Antimatter Systems
companies.description: Antimatter Systems is an education technology company building a peer-to-peer learning network where students demonstrate mastery by making memes, puzzles, and games rather than by writing essays or sitting tests. Founded by Jonathan Libov, the company raised a $2M seed round led by Version One Ventures in 2023, joined by Spacecadet, Ordinary Holdings, Haystack and Compound. Its classroom product lets teachers create meme-based activities with deadlines and instructions, invite students by shareable link, moderate submissions, restrict learners to view-only, work from a library of pre-approved templates, catch unedited-image uploads with plagiarism detection, and grade every submission in one place; the company states it should be free for schools. Antimatter also ships a Sorcerer AI instructional coach plus the consumer Antimatter: Creator and Antimatter: Universe iOS apps. The platform runs on the web at playantimatter.com. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

companies.name: Holberton School
companies.description: Holberton School is a Silicon Valley-born technology education company that trains software and AI engineers through project-based, peer-driven learning rather than traditional lectures. Students build real applications from day one, using AI as a learning partner while developing the collaboration and problem-solving skills employers need, and the school reports a 92% employment rate among alumni. Holberton operates campuses and partner programs globally and delivers curriculum in software engineering, AI/machine learning, cybersecurity, and cloud. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech; the school publishes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface at this time.

companies.name: Lala
companies.description: Lala (meetlala.io) is an AI content platform for educators that turns recordings of online classes into publishable social media content. Instructors either host lessons natively on Lala's own video-call product or upload an existing recording by file or link, and Lala automatically curates short-form Reels in Instagram and TikTok aspect ratios, assembles packaged courses, and returns a transcription and summary after each class. It is sold in three tiers -- Free, Pro and Enterprise -- metered on upload minutes, video-call participants and Reels generated per class, and is aimed at tutors, music instructors, teacherpreneurs, schools and universities. Lala is a 500 Global portfolio company that came out of the 500 Georgia program. As of July 2026 Lala publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API description.

companies.name: Marble Health
companies.description: Marble Health is a virtual mental-health company providing personalized therapy for K-12 students, delivered through partnerships with schools and school districts and directly to families. Licensed therapists meet with students over video, typically within a few days and with no waitlists, and the service accepts most insurance plans including Medicaid. The platform at app.marblehealth.com handles referrals and intake for school counselors and parents, and Marble Health also runs parent workshops and professional-development training for educators. The company is backed by Costanoa Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Marble Health exposes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface (no .well-known documents and no llms.txt); it is a consumer/patient-facing healthtech service rather than an API provider.

companies.name: Quero Educação
companies.description: Quero Educação is a Brazilian education-technology company that operates a marketplace connecting students with higher-education institutions across Brazil. Its flagship product Quero Bolsa lets students compare colleges, courses and schools with price transparency and enroll online at discounted tuition, while a suite of institution-facing products — Nota Quero (online entrance exams), Matrícula Digital (digital enrollment), Quero Pago (tuition payments) and Quero Analytics (data intelligence) — helps partner schools fill seats and manage admissions. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It maintains a private GitHub organization and a public engineering blog on Medium, but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or published API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public identity, domain-security posture, and commercial/legal surfaces.

companies.name: Skillshare
companies.description: Skillshare is a New York City–based online learning community for creators, founded in 2010 by Michael Karnjanaprakorn and Malcolm Ong. The platform hosts thousands of on-demand video classes across creative disciplines — illustration, design, photography, animation, lettering, film, productivity, writing, and business — taught by working creators and industry professionals. Skillshare operates on a paid subscription model (Premium membership) that grants members unlimited access to the class catalog, project-based learning, and a discussion community where students submit class projects for feedback. The company has a teacher revenue-share program in which class creators are paid based on watch time and student enrollments, and runs Skillshare for Teams as a B2B offering for organizations to give employees access to the catalog. Skillshare does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner API, or SDK. The platform's programmatic surface is limited to internal web/mobile clients and an affiliate/marketing referral program; there is no documented developer portal, public webhook system, or third-party integration API for the Skillshare catalog, enrollments, watch-time, or teacher-payout data.

companies.name: Vedantu
companies.description: Vedantu is an Indian online-learning (edtech) company headquartered in Bangalore that delivers LIVE interactive classes, recorded courses, offline centres, and one-to-one tutoring for school students from Class 1 to 12 and competitive-exam aspirants, covering CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE and major State Boards plus JEE, NEET, CUET and Olympiad preparation, alongside a large free library of NCERT solutions, revision notes, sample papers and study material. Backed by Accel, Vedantu is consumer-facing and operates no public developer API today; its only published integration surface is a legacy External-Integration (EI) kit for institutes on GitHub, though it does publish an llms.txt for agents.

companies.name: Recess
companies.description: Recess (Recess Academy, recess.gg) is an online school for gifted and neurodivergent students, including learners with ADHD, dyslexia, autism spectrum, and anxiety. It combines core academics, interest-led classes, small-group coworking sessions with an AI tutor, and a daily community hour, with personalized pacing and world-class mentors. Recess is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer education web application and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; the only machine-discoverable surface found is a valid RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact.

companies.name: Bonum Coaching
companies.description: Bonum Coaching is an enterprise coaching platform based in Latin America that pairs personalized human coaching with technology to develop talent and improve organizational performance. Its offering spans one-to-one executive coaching, group and team coaching, structured mentoring programs, and CLARA, an AI coach-bot for practicing workplace conversations in a safe environment. The company positions itself around democratizing access to coaching, leadership development, talent retention, building a growth culture, and diversity, equity and inclusion, and counts enterprises such as Uber, Davivienda, Farmatodo, and Mi Banco among its clients. Backed by 500 Global, Bonum Coaching is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

companies.name: EduAdvisor
companies.description: EduAdvisor is a Malaysian education platform that helps students compare, plan and apply for tertiary education. It provides course and university comparison tools, scholarship matching, study-abroad guidance, and free education counseling, working directly with 100+ universities and colleges in Malaysia and abroad to streamline applications for prospective students. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. EduAdvisor currently operates as a consumer-facing WordPress web platform with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Jade Autism
companies.description: Jade (Jade ND) is a Brazil-, UAE-, and UK-based education technology company building inclusive digital solutions for neurodivergent children, including those on the autism spectrum (ASD). Its product family includes Jade Edu (personalized-learning software for schools and educators), the Jade App (cognitive-development games for children, with 185,000+ downloads across 179 countries), Jade Astea (eye-tracking technology that assists professionals in evaluating autism-spectrum diagnosis), and Jade Academy (professional-development courses on inclusive and diverse education). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Junto Education
companies.description: Junto is a Berlin-based leadership-development company and a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. Junto delivers cohort-based, live and interactive online training led by certified coaches who previously held senior leadership roles at leading technology companies. Its programs combine the accountability and personal interaction of offline training with the scalability of online learning, and cover first-time managers, high-performance teams, and custom leadership tracks. Junto sells directly to organizations, who nominate high-potential employees for the programs. Junto operates a marketing site at junto.eu and a customer learning application at app.junto.eu. As of this profile, Junto publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Kiko Labs
companies.description: Kiko Labs is a neuroscience-based early-learning company (a 500 Global portfolio company) that builds adaptive brain-training games for children ages 3-7. Its flagship product, Kiko's Thinking Time, is a voice-guided iOS app developed with Harvard and UC Berkeley neuroscientists with support from the US Department of Education and National Science Foundation. The program trains executive functions — working memory, inhibition, focus, and cognitive flexibility — through progressive games, and includes a parent and educator dashboard for tracking skill development. Kiko Labs is a consumer edtech company and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Lyra Health
companies.description: Lyra Health is a Burlingame, California enterprise mental health benefits company founded in 2015 that provides employer-sponsored behavioral health care to more than 20 million members across a network of 30,000+ providers in over 200 countries and territories. The platform combines preventive self-care resources, coaching, evidence-based therapy, medication management, family and pediatric services, and specialized acute care delivered through a benefits-administration model sold to large employers and health plans rather than directly to consumers. Lyra's product surface includes the Lyra App for members, the Lyra Empower AI-powered care platform launched in 2025, Centers of Excellence for pediatric mental health and neurodiversity, a manager coaching program, and a clinical-grade AI guide. Customers include Salesforce, Lululemon, Morgan Stanley, Genentech, Starbucks, JE Dunn, VCA, and the School District of Philadelphia, and in March 2026 the company became Workday Wellness's preferred mental health partner. Lyra acquired pediatric and family mental health provider Bend Health in July 2025. Lyra is led by CEO Jennifer Schulz, with Jenny Gonsalves as Chief Product & Technology Officer, Alethea Varra as Chief Clinical Officer, and co-founder Bob Kocher, MD on the board. The company's revenue model is per-member-per- month employer contracts plus utilization-based clinical billing; Lyra does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or self-service API, and its only public GitHub repository is an internal fork of an unrelated infrastructure module. All employer, member, HRIS/eligibility, SSO, and EHR integrations are negotiated and delivered through the Lyra customer success and implementation teams rather than through a self-serve developer surface.

companies.name: Medley
companies.description: Medley is a leadership development company that delivers group-based executive coaching at enterprise scale, pairing professional coaches with AI-enabled tooling to bring quality and a human touch to Fortune 500 organizations. Founded in 2020 by Edith Cooper and Jordan Taylor, the platform runs curated small-group coaching cohorts focused on trust, empathy, communication, and collaboration to drive organizational transformation. Medley raised a $3.7M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It operates as a B2B services and coaching platform and does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Guide Labs
companies.description: Guide Labs is a product-focused AI research company building a new class of inherently interpretable AI systems and foundation models that humans and domain experts can reliably understand, steer, and debug. Its flagship platform, Clarity, is presented as the first inherently interpretable AI platform and surfaces the internal concepts driving a model's decisions, while its Steerling-8B is presented as the first inherently interpretable large language model. The team has published more than two dozen interpretability papers at top machine-learning venues and ships research artifacts such as PRISM training-data prototypes, the FineWeb Concept Atlas, and Atlas for orienting LLM pre-training data. Access to Clarity is available through platform.guidelabs.ai. The company is backed by Initialized Capital.

companies.name: Laureate Education
companies.description: Laureate Education, Inc. is a for-profit higher-education network founded in 1989 as Sylvan Learning Systems and renamed Laureate Education in May 2004. At its 2017 IPO peak the company operated more than 200 campuses across 28 countries serving over one million students; it became only the third B Corporation to go public when it listed on NASDAQ (ticker: LAUR) on 1 February 2017. Between 2018 and 2021 Laureate executed one of the largest sector-wide divestiture programs in the history of higher education, exiting Brazil (sold to Ânima Holding for ~$765M), the United States (Walden University sold to Adtalem for $1.48B), Australia / New Zealand (sold to Strategic Education), Chile (Universidad Andrés Bello transferred to Fundación Educación y Cultura in September 2020), Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, Malaysia, China, Italy, Cyprus and the United Kingdom — returning $1.29B to shareholders in October 2021. After the divestiture cycle Laureate continued as a pure-play Mexico / Peru operator with five remaining institutions and approximately 460,000 students. In May 2024 the company was acquired by an investor group led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC, a member of the World Bank Group) and Sterling Capital, taking Laureate Education private and delisting it from NASDAQ. The company is headquartered at 1000 Brickell Avenue, Suite 715, Miami, FL. Laureate does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhook surface, or status page. There is no Laureate Education GitHub organization. This profile therefore captures the corporate surface — institutions, divestiture history, leadership, investor status, news — rather than a programmable interface. The five remaining campus-network institutions each publish their own consumer-facing websites (UVM, UNITEC in Mexico; UPC, UPN, Cibertec in Peru) but none expose machine-readable APIs documented from the parent.

companies.name: 2U
companies.description: 2U, Inc. is an education technology company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lanham, Maryland, that partners with the world's top universities and companies to develop and deliver online education programs — from free open courses to bootcamps, certificates, and credit-bearing master's degrees. In 2021 2U acquired edX, which it operates as its global online learning platform and primary consumer brand, offering thousands of courses across subjects such as artificial intelligence, data science, public health, and business. This profile was seeded from a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio-linked lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. 2U publishes no first-party developer API on its corporate domain (2u.com); its programmatic and integration surfaces live under the edX / Open edX learning platform, and its engineering work is visible in the 2uinc GitHub organization.

companies.name: Course Hero
companies.description: Course Hero is an online learning platform where students and educators access more than 25 million course-specific study resources — practice problems, study guides, class notes, step-by-step explanations, essays, and lab reports — alongside 24/7 tutoring and AI-assisted study tools. Founded in 2006 by Andrew Grauer at Cornell University and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Course Hero is part of Learneo, a family of learning and productivity brands that also includes QuillBot, Symbolab, LitCharts, CliffsNotes, Scribbr, Bartleby, and LanguageTool. Course Hero exposes only internal, undocumented web APIs (under /api/) that power its consumer web and mobile apps; it publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or partner API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, Sierra Ventures, and SV Angel.

companies.name: GoGuardian
companies.description: GoGuardian is a K-12 education technology company whose suite - Admin (DNS and device content filtering for CIPA compliance), Teacher (classroom management and student engagement), and Beacon (student safety and self-harm / suicide risk detection) - is administered through web dashboards rather than a broadly published public API. GoGuardian's integration model is primarily roster ingestion - it syncs organizations, students, teachers, guardians, and classes from district Student Information Systems via the IMS Global / 1EdTech OneRoster 1.1 REST API (using a Consumer ID / Secret and a OneRoster URL), Clever, ClassLink, and Google Classroom, and it consumes Google Workspace admin APIs on the district's behalf. A developer / partner documentation portal exists at based.goguardian.com ("GoGuardian Based Docs"), but GoGuardian's own outbound developer API surface is partner-gated and not openly published. The API entries below are honestly modeled logical surfaces, not a confirmed public REST catalog.

companies.name: Mentimeter
companies.description: Mentimeter is a Swedish audience-engagement and interactive-presentation platform used to run live polls, quizzes, word clouds, ranking, open-ended questions and Q&A during meetings, classrooms and events, with results updating in real time as participants respond from their phones. Founded in Stockholm in 2014, it is used across education and enterprise for interactive presentations and workshops. Mentimeter does not publish a public developer REST API; its extensibility surface is delivered through LMS integrations (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Brightspace via LTI), presentation add-ins (PowerPoint, Microsoft Teams, Zoom) and SSO, rather than a documented HTTP API. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline against its public developer, security and trust surface.

companies.name: Physics Wallah
companies.description: Physics Wallah (PW) is India's leading affordable education technology platform, offering live and recorded courses, test series, notes, and doubt-solving for competitive exams (IIT JEE, NEET, GATE, UPSC), government job preparation (SSC, Banking, Railways, Defence), school boards (CBSE, ICSE, and regional boards), and professional certifications (CA, CS, CFA, ACCA). Beyond its flagship pw.live learning app it operates PW Skills for professional upskilling, PW Store for books and study material, CuriousJr for younger grades, and 100+ offline Vidyapeeth and Pathshala centres across 175+ cities. Physics Wallah reached unicorn status in 2022 and serves tens of millions of students. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Physics Wallah does not publish an official public developer portal or API program; the company's public technology footprint is a set of open-source infrastructure libraries under its tech-pw GitHub org.

companies.name: PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers)
companies.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms, with approximately 370,000 staff across a global network of member firms coordinated by PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL). PwC organizes delivery across three primary service lines — Assurance (audit), Tax (tax compliance, planning, and reporting), and Advisory (consulting, deals, and risk). The firm operates proprietary technology platforms including PwC Halo (a suite of data analytics tools used to support audit engagements), the Trusted AI initiative (PwC's responsible-AI governance and assurance framework), and ProEdge (a workforce upskilling platform). In April 2024 PwC announced a multi-year alliance with OpenAI positioning the firm as both OpenAI's largest customer and its first reseller of ChatGPT Enterprise, supporting PwC's broader generative-AI consulting practice. PwC's research and insights surface — pwc.com/insights, the annual Global CEO Survey, the Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey, the Money Tree report, and regional industry outlooks — is the firm's primary public-facing knowledge product. PwC does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, partner API documentation, or a GitHub organization at the corporate level. The github.com/pwc handle is held by an unrelated individual user (Patrick Clearwater). Any technical integrations with PwC platforms are arranged through engagement contracts and the PwC Technology Consulting practice rather than through self-service developer credentials. PwC's content distribution is reader-facing (newsletter subscriptions, the PwC US Newsroom, LinkedIn, YouTube) with no documented public RSS feed endpoint exposing news, press releases, or insights as a syndication contract.

companies.name: Remind
companies.description: Remind is a K-12 school-home communication platform that lets teachers, schools, and districts message students and families by text, app, email, and voice without exchanging personal phone numbers. The product line includes Remind Chat, a free two-way messaging service used by individual teachers and classrooms, and Remind Hub, a paid district-wide communications platform with administrative controls, SIS integration, delivery analytics, and translation into 90+ languages. Remind reports use in roughly 80% of US public schools and by a majority of US teachers. In November 2023, Santa Barbara-based ParentSquare acquired Remind, and the combined company now operates under the ParentSquare name with Remind Hub continuing for existing district customers and Remind Chat continuing for classroom-level use; Remind Tutoring was discontinued as part of the combination. Remind's only externally documented developer surface is the Share on Remind SDK (the "Remind Share SDK"), a partner program that lets approved third-party content providers embed the Remind composer into their own product, authenticate Remind users via OAuth 2.0, serve shareable content and previews via partner-hosted webhooks, and ship messages back through Remind. The Share SDK is accessed by application through partners@remind.com and the developer console at remind.com/integrations; there is no public self-serve REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no general-purpose messaging API for sending Remind messages from third-party systems.

companies.name: Unacademy
companies.description: Unacademy is a Bangalore-based online learning platform — one of India's largest — offering live classes, courses, study material, and test preparation for competitive exams including UPSC Civil Services, IIT JEE, NEET-UG, SSC, CA Foundation, and CSIR UGC NET, delivered through its web platform and dedicated learner, educator, and parent mobile apps. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Unacademy runs a consumer platform on an internal API (api.unacademy.com) but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Hudl
companies.description: Hudl is a Lincoln, Nebraska sports performance and analytics technology company founded in 2007. The company started as a video sharing and review platform for high school, college, and professional teams and has grown into a global provider of video capture hardware, performance analysis software, and sports data services. Hudl operates across basketball, baseball, football, ice hockey, rugby, soccer, softball, and volleyball, serving customers from youth clubs through professional leagues. The company's product portfolio spans the core Hudl video platform, Hudl Focus AI-powered capture cameras (Indoor, Outdoor, Flex, Point), Hudl Replay and Hudl Studio for live and tactical analysis, Hudl IQ for American football analytics, Volleymetrics, the Hudl TV livestreaming product, and Hudl Tickets digital ticketing. Through acquisitions Hudl has consolidated several leading performance analysis and football data brands under its umbrella, including Sportscode (performance analysis software), Wyscout (the largest soccer video and stats database), Statsbomb (advanced football analytics), Instat (video and scouting), WIMU and Titan (athlete tracking and wearables), and Signal and ADI. Hudl exposes commercial developer surfaces primarily through Hudl Wyscout (Wyscout Data API, documented as OpenAPI 3.0 at apidocs.wyscout.com, with Database, Stats, Events, and Physical Data packs) and Hudl Statsbomb (the Statsbomb Aggregated API for player-match, player-season, team-match, and team-season data, accessed via the Data Hub, plus the Raw X&Y Tracking Data API and a Wyscout/Statsbomb ID Mapping API). Core Hudl video and Hudl Focus do not publish a public developer API; B2B integrations are sales-mediated. Hudl maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/hudl) with infrastructure, resilience, and media tooling open source projects (Mjolnir, Fargo, HudlFfmpeg, react-native components), but these are engineering libraries, not product SDKs. Hudl's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions for video, analytics, and data packages, plus camera hardware sales and data licensing.

companies.name: MyARC Fitness
companies.description: MyARC (operated by Vert Analytics Limited) is an all-in-one platform that lets fitness creators and coaches scale their business without writing code. Coaches use MyARC to launch a branded mobile app, automate AI-personalized workout and meal plans for thousands of members at once, run challenges and 1-on-1 coaching, build community, and earn recurring subscription revenue. The consumer-facing MyARC Fitness app ships on iOS and Android with progress tracking and accountability features. As of this profile MyARC exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a creator-facing SaaS and mobile product, not an API provider. Offices in London, New York, Melbourne, and India.

companies.name: Myu
companies.description: Myu (MyU Interactive Learning) is an education-technology company offering an integrated learning management system (LMS) and school management platform that unifies class delivery, a student information system (SIS), grading and academic reporting, attendance and compliance tracking, and parent/teacher communication in a single interface. It serves early-childhood centers, K-12 schools, higher-education institutions, training institutes, and individual teachers across 1,000+ institutions worldwide, with a notable presence in the GCC region. Myu is delivered as web and mobile (iOS/Android) applications and, as of this profiling, exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Study Edge
companies.description: Study Edge is an education technology company that builds online learning, tutoring, and test-preparation platforms for students. Its products deliver on-demand instructional video, live and scheduled study sessions, practice problems, and course-specific study resources, and the company is known for operating statewide math learning platforms such as Algebra Nation / Math Nation. Study Edge is a consumer- and institution-facing learning service rather than a developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company.

companies.name: Swing Education
companies.description: Swing Education is a technology-driven substitute teacher staffing marketplace for K-12 schools and districts across the United States. Its vetted platform connects schools and districts with qualified, background-checked substitute teachers and classified staff to cover daily absences, long-term leaves, special education classrooms, and paraprofessional roles. Schools request coverage through an online admin console while substitutes browse and claim assignments through a dedicated app. The company reports a 94% fill rate, an average five-minute fill time, and coverage of more than 6,000 schools. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the public site exposes no developer/API surface, so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Admission Table
companies.description: Admission Table (admissiontable.com) was a study-abroad and overseas-education counseling platform founded in 2013 by Manish Katyan and Duleep Deosthale, offering real-time student counseling, university admissions guidance, scholarships, financing, and online test preparation for the SAT, GRE, GMAT, TOEFL, and IELTS. It was backed by 500 Global, NYU, and Aarin Capital, and was subsequently acquired by Azent Overseas Education. The admissiontable.com domain now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to azent.com. This entry was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no public API, developer program, or API documentation on either host, so no API artifacts were produced.

companies.name: Age of Learning
companies.description: Age of Learning, Inc. is a Glendale, California educational technology company founded in 2007, best known for ABCmouse.com Early Learning Academy, a subscription digital curriculum for children ages 2-8, along with Adventure Academy (ages 8-13) and Mastery-branded school programs. It builds direct-to-consumer and school-facing learning products delivered through web and mobile apps (iOS and Android). Age of Learning does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a consumer edtech provider surfaced from the ICONIQ Capital portfolio, enriched with the public link surface (privacy, terms, support, press, careers) and a domain-security posture probed from public DNS/TLS records.

companies.name: Arivihan
companies.description: Arivihan is an Indian EdTech company operating an AI-based, fully automated online learning platform that gives each K-12 school student a personalized "tutor in their pocket." It targets low- and middle-income families and students in Tier 2+ cities, delivering interactive, personalized lectures and doubt resolution in vernacular languages at roughly 10% of typical coaching fees. Products include the DoubtBuzzter mobile app and the tutor-prod / InstantGuru doubt-resolution web platform. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and prosus-ventures. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this remains a consumer-facing product profile.

companies.name: Chegg.com
companies.description: Chegg, Inc. is a US-based education technology company that provides direct-to-student learning services on a subscription basis, including homework and expert Q&A help, step-by-step textbook and problem solutions, textbook rental and purchase, online tutoring, writing and citation tools, math and science solvers, and AI-assisted study support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass Chegg publishes a consumer web and mobile product but no public developer portal, documented API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server; this profile therefore captures its public web identity and domain-security posture only.

companies.name: CodeMentor
companies.description: CodeMentor (codementor.io) is an on-demand marketplace that connects software developers with vetted expert mentors for live 1:1 coding help, code review, debugging, pair programming, and longer-term freelance engagements across dozens of programming languages and frameworks. Part of the Arc / CodeMentor group, it serves individual learners seeking real-time mentorship as well as companies hiring vetted remote developers. As of this profile CodeMentor exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this record was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with verified identity and domain-security signals.

companies.name: EDUFI PTE. LTD
companies.description: EduFi (EDUFI PTE. LTD) is a Singapore-incorporated education-financing fintech operating Pakistan's first Study Now, Pay Later (SNPL) digital platform, with expansion into Saudi Arabia and Oman. The Shariah-approved platform lets parents and students finance private schooling, higher education, and international student loans through quick, collateral-free approvals with direct disbursement to educational institutes and convenient monthly installments. EduFi also provides partner educational institutes a free ERP system and subsidized SNPL for their students, and works with financial institutions to fund receivables. Backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist; EduFi publishes a consumer marketing and application surface but no public developer/API program.

companies.name: Four Pillars
companies.description: Four Pillars is a research-driven blockchain enterprise headquartered in Asia, operating through three divisions: FP Research publishes primary analysis of crypto protocols, markets, and policy with deep regional expertise across Korea and the broader Asian market; FP Validated runs validator and node infrastructure across proof-of-stake networks, pairing research with live operations; and FP Institution advises banks, financial institutions, and corporates on blockchain strategy. The firm serves founders, funds, and regulators, and is a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. It is a research and advisory business rather than a developer-facing API platform, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: GoStudent
companies.description: GoStudent is an online tutoring platform headquartered in Vienna, Austria, offering personalized one-on-one lessons across 30+ subjects for K-12 and university students. Founded in 2016, it matches learners with vetted tutors and delivers lessons through its own video-classroom apps for iOS, Android, and web, sold as a monthly subscription. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and Speedinvest, GoStudent grew into one of Europe's largest edtech companies and has acquired peers including Tus Media, Seneca Learning, and Studienkreis. GoStudent does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web properties and domain-security posture as a network lead.

companies.name: Guild Education
companies.description: Guild is an education benefits platform that helps large employers turn workforce education into workforce strategy. Guild connects a company's frontline and hourly workers to a curated marketplace of debt-free education, upskilling, and career-development programs delivered through vetted learning partners (universities, bootcamps, and skilling providers), and pairs that access with coaching and analytics so HR leaders can fill critical roles, improve retention, increase internal mobility, and prove measurable ROI. Guild operates as a B2B2C platform: employers fund and administer the benefit, learning partners supply the programs, and members (employees) enroll and progress toward degrees, certificates, and new durable skills. Guild does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public company and web-property surface.

companies.name: Herb
companies.description: Herb (herb.co) is a leading digital media and e-commerce platform dedicated to cannabis culture, education, and lifestyle. It publishes cannabis news, strain databases, product reviews, dispensary and brand guides, deals, recipes, and city-level legalization guides, and operates the "Herb Agency" offering branding and marketing services to cannabis companies. The consumer site is built on Gatsby (React) with a GraphQL data layer, Algolia search, and a Firebase/serverless backend hosted on Netlify. Herb is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio; the company exposes no public developer API program at this time, so this profile captures its published web, content, and discovery surface (llms.txt, domain security posture, and identity/link properties) rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: IMP Software
companies.description: IMP Software builds MAT-first financial management software for the UK education sector. Its flagship product, IMP Planner, is a single-database, trust-wide platform for budgeting, forecasting, reporting, Integrated Curriculum Financial Planning (ICFP) and purchasing, used by Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) and their schools. Based in Exeter, UK, the company is trusted by more than 550 trusts across roughly 6,000 schools and secured a growth investment from Partech in September 2025. IMP Planner is a closed SaaS application for trust finance teams; IMP Software does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Iris.ai
companies.description: Iris.ai is a Norwegian AI company providing an AI knowledge foundation for regulated enterprises, turning complex enterprise and scientific data into trustworthy, compliant AI. Its platform spans three products — Axion (data organization for AI-ready intelligence), Neuralith (enterprise knowledge integration into AI engines), and RSpace, the Researcher Workspace that lets R&D teams, librarians, and academics search, filter, analyze, extract, summarize, and report across scientific literature. Iris.ai is backed by 500 Global. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture pending any future developer surface.

companies.name: La Solive
companies.description: La Solive is a French vocational training organization (organisme de formation) preparing career-changers and apprentices for the trades behind building energy renovation and the climate transition. It runs state-recognized, practice-based programs — chef de projet en rénovation énergétique, conducteur de travaux, plombier chauffagiste pompe à chaleur et gaz, technicien de maintenance CVC, installateur de panneaux photovoltaïques, QualiPAC and agent de maintenance du bâtiment — delivered across campuses in Paris, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Toulouse and Lille plus a distance-learning track, with Qualiopi certification and France Travail / Mon Compte Formation / Transitions Pro financing. La Solive reports 1,500+ students trained and 500+ recruiting partner companies. It is a Partech portfolio company in the Climate sector. As of this enrichment pass La Solive publishes no public API, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it does publish an /llms.txt agent-readable site index, captured in this repo.

companies.name: Lovevery
companies.description: Lovevery is a direct-to-consumer children's brand that designs stage-based Play Kits, books, and learning products for infants and toddlers, grounded in child-development research. It operates a Shopify-backed e-commerce and subscription storefront at lovevery.com with a customer help center, blog, and careers site. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network, Lovevery publishes no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Mentor Collective
companies.description: Mentor Collective operates an AI Mentorship OS for higher education, powering peer mentoring, student success, and retention programs at colleges and universities. Its platform matches and onboards mentors and mentees, guides conversations with AI prompts, surfaces risk signals and belonging gaps, and turns connection data into real-time retention intelligence for institutions. Backed by Techstars, the company serves higher-education and workforce partners. As of this profile Mentor Collective publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this repo captures its public web, blog, legal, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Oboe
companies.description: Oboe is an AI-powered learning platform whose mission is to teach one billion people one trillion things. Positioned as "AI that won't make you stupid," it lets anyone learn virtually any subject through a conversational interface that generates personalized, on-demand courses and lessons ("magical courses made just for you"). Founded in New York and backed by Homebrew, Oboe is building what it calls the world's first completely generalized AI-powered learning platform, focused on making humans smarter rather than only making machines smarter. As a consumer web application, Oboe does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; api.oboe.com serves only an XML sitemap index for public course pages.

companies.name: Peak
companies.description: Peak is a consumer brain-training mobile application operated by Synaptic Labs (formerly Peak Labs) that offers cognitive exercise games and personalized workouts spanning memory, attention, problem-solving, mental agility, language, and emotion. Its games and Advanced Training Programmes are developed with researchers from institutions including Cambridge, Yale, UCL, and King's College London. Peak Pro is a subscription that unlocks 40+ games, personalized workouts, performance analytics, and an AI Coach. Peak is a mobile-only consumer product distributed via the App Store and Google Play and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

companies.name: Poker Skill
companies.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.

companies.name: Quantum Circuits
companies.description: Quantum Circuits, Inc. is a quantum computing hardware company (a Yale University spinout) building superconducting quantum systems with built-in error detection. Its dual-rail cavity qubits pair Quantum Error Detection (QED), Real-Time Control Flow (RTCF), and Error Detection Handling (EDH), and its Aqumen Seeker QPU (introduced November 2024) targets stable, repeatable, fault-tolerant quantum computation. The company engages early users through a Strategic Quantum Release (SQR) program that includes a simulator and access to Aqumen Seeker systems, rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Saturn
companies.description: Saturn is a mobile calendar and scheduling app built for high school students, designed around the complexities of the school day, built around your friends, and kept truly real-time. Students import their class schedule, see what their friends are doing, coordinate activities, and share their calendar socially. The company positions itself as "the next generation calendar, enabling time together for all." Saturn is a consumer iOS and Android application distributed through the App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by General Catalyst and Insight Partners, with notable individual investors including Jeff Bezos, Marc Benioff, and Dara Khosrowshahi.

companies.name: Seekho
companies.description: Seekho (operated by Keyaro Edutech Pvt Ltd, Bengaluru, India) is a consumer edutainment mobile application delivering short-form learning videos across 50+ categories including stock market investing, spoken English, YouTube monetization, business, cooking, and government-procedure (sarkari) guidance. The platform reports 10 crore+ downloads, 40+ lakh learners, 10,000+ videos, and 250+ verified mentors, and is distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass, Seekho publishes a consumer marketing site, a blog, and a creator program but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or partner API surface.

companies.name: The Mind Company
companies.description: The Mind Company is a consumer mental-fitness company that builds a multi-app platform for cognitive and emotional wellbeing. Its apps include Elevate (cognitive training across memory, vocabulary, math, and more), Balance (personalized meditation for sleep, stress, and focus), and Spark (puzzle-based learning). The company is a portfolio company of Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a direct-to-consumer mobile app business, The Mind Company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed security posture.

companies.name: pandas
companies.description: pandas is a fast, powerful, flexible, and easy to use open source data analysis and manipulation tool, built on top of the Python programming language. It is a Python library that provides DataFrame and Series data structures and analysis tools; pandas itself does not expose an HTTP API, but is widely used to build data APIs alongside frameworks like FastAPI and Flask.

companies.name: Erudifi
companies.description: ErudiFi (ErudiFi Pte. Ltd., formerly Dana Cita Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-registered company) is an education-financing technology company on a mission to expand access to affordable financial services for students across Southeast Asia. It operates two consumer lending platforms: Bukas in the Philippines, which provides secure, integrated tuition installment plans in partnership with top colleges and universities, and Danacita in Indonesia, a peer-to-peer education-financing platform registered with the OJK that funds diploma, bachelor's, master's, and short-course programs. ErudiFi is backed by investors including 500 Global and Helicap. The company maintains a small public GitHub presence (internal tooling, a data-quality checker, and a Danacita UI kit) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP server.

companies.name: Honorlock
companies.description: Honorlock is an online exam proctoring and academic integrity platform for higher education and professional certification. Its primary integration path is LTI 1.3, installed natively into LMS platforms - Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, D2L Brightspace, Open LMS, Docebo, and Intellum - plus publisher platforms such as Pearson, McGraw Hill, and ALEKS via LMS workflows. For assessment platforms that need to embed proctoring outside an LMS, Honorlock offers a partner developer toolkit ("APIs and Elements") documented at docs.honorlock.com - a REST API for provisioning users, courses, exams, authentication tokens, and exam sessions, plus a browser-based Elements/Integration SDK that drives the exam-taker experience (extension verification, session setup, begin/end session). The developer program is sales-gated (contact-sales onboarding); Honorlock does not publish a self-service API key flow, an OpenAPI description, or a public base URL.

companies.name: Level AI
companies.description: Level AI (legally Ujwal Inc.) is a Mountain View, California contact center AI company founded in 2019 by Ashish Nagar, a former member of Amazon's Alexa conversational AI team. The company builds LLM-native customer experience intelligence and service automation for enterprise contact centers, with a platform spanning two product surfaces: a CX Delivery suite (AI Virtual Agent, Agent Assist, AgentGPT, Coaching, Manager Assist, Knowledge Bot, Auto Summary, Agent Screen Recording) and a CX Strategy suite (Auto-QA on 100% of interactions, Voice of the Customer theme detection, omnichannel Analytics, iCSAT, AI Workers). The proprietary full-stack AI platform includes Level AI's own ASR/Voice AI and semantic-intelligence layer trained on customer-service data, and is positioned for financial services, insurance, healthcare, retail, banking, and collections operations. Level AI exposes a public REST API for bidirectional data exchange with BI tools and existing contact center stacks, and ships native integrations across telephony, CRM, customer support, workforce management, CX management, communication, learning management, and SSO categories. The company has raised $73.1M to date (Series A 2021, Series B 2022 led by Battery Ventures, Series C $39.4M 2024 led by Adams Street Partners with Cross Creek, Brightloop, Battery Ventures and Eniac Ventures), holds a 4.7/5 rating on G2, and reports customer outcomes including 25% CSAT lift, 45% agent satisfaction improvement, and 90% time savings on manual QA. The Level AI GitHub organization (github.com/Level-AI) exists but is currently empty — there is no public OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source release; the API is documented and credentialed through the customer's tenant of the Level AI platform.

companies.name: MasteryConnect
companies.description: MasteryConnect is a K-12 formative assessment and standards-mastery platform, now part of Instructure. It helps teachers and districts build standards-aligned assessments (from prebuilt items or custom content), deliver common and benchmark assessments, auto-score results, and turn the data into intuitive mastery reports that guide interventions. It integrates tightly with the Canvas LMS through single sign-on and real-time data synchronization. MasteryConnect was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; it was acquired by Instructure in 2019 and does not publish a standalone public developer API — integration is delivered through the Canvas LMS platform and its REST API.

companies.name: beva
companies.description: beva (贝瓦网), operated by ProKids Technology Corp / 芝兰玉树（北京）科技股份有限公司, is a Chinese IP-and-technology driven family education and entertainment company. Its flagship original IP is the little beaver "Beva" (贝瓦) and the "Beva Children's Songs" (贝瓦儿歌) brand, spanning children's music, animation, literature and interactive entertainment, distributed across web, mobile, OTT, IPTV and television channels. Through its ProKids Copyright Content Open Platform (open.beva.com) beva offers online-application and offline content-access APIs that let third-party mobile apps and smart hardware — story machines, smart speakers and kids' robots such as MiTu, Rokid and the Doraemon story machine — embed licensed children's audio and video content. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

companies.name: Echo Labs
companies.description: Echo Labs is a San Francisco-based company building AI-powered media accessibility for higher education. Its platform audits, captions, and audio describes entire institutional video libraries within 24 hours, producing ADA / Title II and WCAG 2.1 AA compliant closed captions and audio descriptions at claimed accuracy above 99 percent and roughly $0.75 per minute — a fraction of legacy vendor pricing. Echo integrates with major learning management systems (7+ LMS platforms) so universities and colleges can bring existing course video into compliance at institutional scale. The company is SOC 2 certified, completed a pre-seed round, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This API Evangelist profile tracks Echo Labs as a company in the network; the provider does not publish a public API or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Kenbi
companies.description: Kenbi is a German healthcare organization focused on nursing education and workforce development, operating through two divisions. Kenbi Academy delivers continuing professional development for care workers with 100+ ZFU-certified courses recognized by all German health insurers and available nationwide, spanning nursing service management, quality assurance, wound care, and instructor training. Kenbi Campus runs vocational nursing programs in Berlin and Hamburg, including a three-year registered nurse generalist program and an 18-month nursing assistant curriculum. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found.

companies.name: Sequence Bio
companies.description: Sequence Bio is a life sciences and population genomics company based in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, focused on discovering the genetic causes of disease to power the development of new medicines. The company leverages the founder-effect genetics of the Newfoundland and Labrador population, running a large-scale Study of the Genetic Causes of Inherited Disease to identify novel drug targets and predictors of treatment response for pharmaceutical partners. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a corporate and research website but does not currently expose a public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Answers.com
companies.description: Answers.com is a consumer question-and-answer and reference website where visitors ask questions and get instant answers across trivia, science, history, and everyday topics, increasingly blended with AI-personality chat, flashcard makers, study guides, and a math solver. It operates as a content and reference destination rather than a developer platform, and the enrichment pipeline found no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile is retained as a company record in the API Evangelist network; the only machine-verifiable artifact is a live domain-security probe of the answers.com host.

companies.name: Comento
companies.description: Comento is a South Korean career development and mentoring platform based in Seoul that connects job seekers with working professionals. The service offers a Q&A community and timeline for career discussions, free unlimited mentoring questions answered by industry practitioners, resume and cover letter (자기소개서) review, an AI resume analyzer, interview preparation, and job-focused educational programs including bootcamps (직무부트캠프) and classes for the Korean job market. It also runs corporate training and university affiliation partnerships. Comento operates as a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched with the domain and identity signals that are publicly observable.

companies.name: Crossfit
companies.description: CrossFit is a fitness brand and training methodology built around constantly varied, high-intensity functional movements that combine strength, conditioning, gymnastics, and weightlifting. The organization operates a global network of independently owned affiliate gyms, delivers a coaching certification and education program (the Level 1 through Level 4 courses and specialty seminars), and produces the annual CrossFit Games competition season. CrossFit was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer and affiliate web presence (gym finder, courses, store, Games results) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition.

companies.name: Doomersion
companies.description: Doomersion (doomlingo.ai) is a consumer mobile language-learning app that teaches languages by "doomscrolling" — a vertical, TikTok-style feed of short-form videos in the learner's target language, matched to their level, with clickable explainer subtitles that let you tap any word for an instant translation and grammar note. Founded by Mostafa Afr and backed by Y Combinator, the app ships on iOS and Android. Doomersion exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record is an API Evangelist network company profile capturing its public web and identity footprint.

companies.name: Fidu
companies.description: Fidu is an operating system and financial-services platform for private K-12 schools across Spanish-speaking Latin America. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Fidu digitizes the academic, administrative, financial, and communication processes of educational institutions in a single platform. School administrators send tuition statements and pay slips to families, who then pay tuition directly through the Fidu mobile app, and a "Parent Copilot" AI layer handles 24/7 automated responses, content generation, and academic-data synchronization with school information systems. Fidu raised a $5M seed round led by NFX and Lightspeed Venture Partners and reports more than 1,000 institutions across 10 countries and over 500,000 active users. Fidu does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures the company's real public web properties only.

companies.name: Marriage Pact
companies.description: Marriage Pact is a matchmaking platform that pairs people using a research-backed compatibility questionnaire, originally built for college campuses and run as periodic matching events across universities. Participants answer a values-and-preferences survey and the service uses the responses to compute and deliver each person their most compatible match. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures, the company operates as a consumer web product; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or programmatic integration surface.

companies.name: OpenDurian
companies.description: OpenDurian is a Bangkok, Thailand based educational technology company delivering hybrid (online plus offline) learning and test preparation. Its platform offers exam-prep courses for TOEIC, IELTS, TOEFL, TCAS and Thai civil-service exams, language instruction in English, Chinese and Japanese, secondary-school mathematics and science courses, an online bookstore, free English-proficiency assessment tools, and extensive practice-test question banks. The company reports reach in the millions of annual users across its learning ecosystem. It is a consumer-facing edtech product; as of this enrichment pass no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found.

companies.name: Openhouse
companies.description: Openhouse is a network of neighborhood children's learning centres in Bangalore and Kolkata, India, describing itself as a "Third Space" for children — neither home nor school, but a sanctuary for curiosity.
