Founded by experts in AI systems, analog circuits, computing theory, and neuroscience, and backed by Playground Global, the company researches dynamical-systems computing substrates — coupled-oscillator (Kuramoto) hardware, an instruction set architecture for dynamical-system hardware, and hardware/software neural co-evolution — targeting biology-scale energy efficiency. Its open-source Un-0 model generates images with simulated coupled oscillators. Unconventional does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or hosted product.

companies.name: Unconventional AI
companies.description: Unconventional AI is rethinking the foundations of compute to bring biology-scale energy efficiency to AI. The company researches dynamical systems such as coupled Kuramoto oscillators as a computing substrate that maps onto analog and physical hardware, pointing toward on the order of 1000x lower energy for AI than today's digital accelerators. Its open-source Un-0 reference implementation generates images by integrating the phase dynamics of coupled oscillators. Backed by DCVC, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Lux Capital, and Wing Venture Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Knowmia.com
companies.description: Knowmia was an education-focused video platform used by instructors to create, share, and assign instructional video and lessons. The brand was operated by TechSmith alongside Camtasia and Snagit, and was marketed as Knowmia and Knowmia Pro for classroom and campus video. TechSmith retired Knowmia Pro in early 2025 and now directs former Knowmia customers to TechSmith Screencast, which offers comparable asynchronous video sharing, commenting, and review and integrates with Snagit and Camtasia. As of July 2026 knowmia.com issues an HTTP 301 redirect to the TechSmith Screencast product page. Knowmia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or machine-readable specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a retired/absorbed entry for historical and lineage purposes.

companies.name: Caraway Health *
companies.description: Caraway Health is a digital health company that provides virtual mental and physical healthcare designed for college and university students, delivered through a mobile app with support offered around the clock. The company partners with higher-education institutions and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). It operates as a direct-to-consumer / campus telehealth provider rather than an API platform; at the time of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification was found on its public web surface. Sector: life-sciences / digital health.

companies.name: Ginger
companies.description: Ginger (formerly Ginger.io) was a behavioral and emotional health company offering on-demand mental health support — coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — delivered through a mobile app and an employer/health-plan benefits model. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead, Ginger merged with Headspace in 2021 to form Headspace Health; the ginger.com domain now redirects to Headspace for Organizations (organizations.headspace.com). Enrichment probing on 2026-07-19 found no independent public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface — every /.well-known path resolves to a soft-404 Headspace marketing page. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; the only genuine machine-derivable artifact is the live domain-security posture of ginger.com.

companies.name: Graham Holdings
companies.description: Graham Holdings (NYSE: GHC) is a diversified holding company with operations in education, television broadcasting, digital media, manufacturing, healthcare, automotive, restaurants, and custom framing. Principal subsidiaries include Kaplan (educational services), Graham Media Group and Social News Desk (broadcasting and social media tools), The Slate Group and Foreign Policy (digital publishing), Code3 and City Cast (digital marketing and local news), Hoover Treated Wood Products, Joyce/Dayton, Group Dekko, and Forney (manufacturing), Graham Healthcare Group (home health and hospice), Graham Automotive (dealerships), Clyde's Restaurant Group (including Old Ebbitt Grill), and Framebridge (online custom framing). No public developer APIs have been identified across the portfolio.

companies.name: Harris Computer
companies.description: Harris Computer is a constellation of companies acquiring and operating vertical market software businesses across the public sector, healthcare, utilities, financial services, education, and insurance markets. Harris Computer itself does not publish a unified public developer portal; APIs and integrations are delivered through its individual portfolio companies (such as Harris Local Government, Harris Utilities, Harris Healthcare, and Harris School Solutions). Harris Computer is a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc.

companies.name: Ornikar
companies.description: Ornikar is a French online driving school and insurance company that guides consumers from earning their driving permit through to car, home, and pet insurance. Founded in France, it offers highway-code (code de la route) training, driving lessons, accelerated permit programs, point-recovery courses, and corporate road-safety training, alongside auto, home, and pet insurance products and CPF financing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: Consumer. No public developer API surface was found during the enrichment pass; only domain-security signals were probed.

companies.name: Traderion
companies.description: Traderion is a fintech company that combines technology and gamification to build digital learning platforms for banks and financial institutions. Its products include a gamified sales and trading simulator covering equities, FX, bonds, and commodities with AI-powered feedback, a MiFID II regulatory-compliance training platform built as a virtual simulated bank, and a risk-profiling platform for identifying and detecting risky behavioral patterns within organizations. A Seedcamp portfolio company, Traderion does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

companies.name: Yacob
companies.description: Yacob was a Dubai-based Intelligent Nutrition platform and 500 Global portfolio company that combined cashless school-meal payments with nutrition monitoring. Pupils paid for school meals with a stored-value card while parents topped up accounts online, tracked transactions in real time, set spend and food limits, flagged allergies, and reviewed the nutritional value of their children's meals. The company appears dormant, with yacob.com no longer resolving as of 2026, and no public API surface was ever found.

companies.name: Blue Studios
companies.description: Blue Studios Labs is a family-focused technology company operating under the tagline "Where Families Flourish." It builds consumer digital products that help couples and families explore, learn, and grow together. Its portfolio includes Wallio, a shared financial-management app for couples and families; Blue Studios EDU, an entertainment-based educational streaming service; and Blue Studios Entertainment, a media-production studio creating family-oriented narratives and content. The company reports more than 400 million digital views, 350,000 game plays, and 4,000+ classes delivered. Blue Studios is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Miruvor AI Inc.
companies.description: Miruvor AI Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech AI research lab building brain-inspired continual learning models. Rather than scaling frozen, pre-trained models, Miruvor uses spiking neural networks as its representational substrate together with local learning rules to build systems that learn from experience in real time, with persistent memory and low-energy, neuromorphic efficiency. Founded out of The Residency and backed by 500 Global, the company is pre-product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: Wikifarmer
companies.description: Wikifarmer is a global agricultural platform that connects producers with buyers through a B2B marketplace for agricultural products and educates farmers through expert-reviewed content. It provides practical agricultural knowledge, market access, and price insights for farmers, agribusinesses, traders, and food companies worldwide, with a multilingual educational library covering crop cultivation, livestock, sustainability, soil management, irrigation, pest control, and post-harvest handling, alongside a global marketplace connecting suppliers and buyers and a price-insights service for agricultural commodities.

companies.name: Altera
companies.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

companies.name: Atom Computing
companies.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

companies.name: Blubblub
companies.description: Blub Blub Inc. is the company behind Speech Blubs, a speech-therapy and language-development app for children aged 1 to 8. Created by speech-language pathologists and child-development experts, the app uses video modeling, speech exercises, face filters, and play-based activities to help kids with speech delays, autism, Down syndrome, and apraxia learn to talk. Speech Blubs is available on iOS and Android, supports English, Spanish, and German, and has been downloaded by over 10 million families worldwide. Blub Blub is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This is a consumer mobile-app company; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so the entry is limited to verified company identity and published web properties.

companies.name: Experiential Labs
companies.description: Experiential Labs is an applied AI research laboratory (Y Combinator Summer 2026, San Francisco) building world models that let AI agents simulate reality with high fidelity. Founded by Kion Fallah (former staff research scientist at Waabi) and Silen Naihin (AutoGPT and agent-benchmark contributor, co-founder of Stackwise), the company adapts techniques from autonomous-vehicle development to reconstruct environments at high accuracy and pursue recursive self-improvement and continual learning across domains. Its public work is open source on GitHub, including the world-model-harness (world-model-as-a-harness for simulating AI agent environments), OpenCLaaS (Continual Learning as a Service), and autoresearch-distillation. The company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Jewelbots
companies.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

companies.name: Knowable
companies.description: Knowable was a mobile audio-learning company that united world-class experts, thinkers, and storytellers to produce structured audio courses for curious minds — an "audio courses" take on online learning delivered as serialized lessons rather than one-off podcasts. Founded by the Bit Kitchen team and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z led its round in May 2019), Knowable published expert-led course series across business, creativity, and personal development. The company is no longer operational: knowable.fyi now serves a tombstone notice stating that Knowable has been acquired by Medium and directing former listeners to Medium.com. Knowable never published a public developer program, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its GitHub organization (bitkitchen) exposes no public repositories. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record from the a16z portfolio; there is no live API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Lego
companies.description: The LEGO Group is a Danish toy company and the world's largest manufacturer of interlocking plastic building bricks. The company extends its brand across video games, theme parks, movies, educational products, and licensed sets for children and adults. LEGO does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; consumer-facing systems and partner integrations are closed. A public GitHub organization hosts internal engineering tooling and open-source contributions.

companies.name: LessonLeap
companies.description: LessonLeap was a group-learning platform for children, offering small-group online classes and tutoring aimed at helping kids keep learning outside of school. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. LessonLeap has since been acquired by Preply, the language-learning and tutoring marketplace, and no longer operates as an independent product. lessonleap.com now serves only a single-page acquisition notice directing visitors to Preply. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no developer portal, no documentation, no API, no SDKs or packages, no public GitHub repositories, and no published .well-known discovery documents — this profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an API provider.

companies.name: LookSharp
companies.description: LookSharp (formerly InternMatch) was the largest internship and entry-level jobs marketplace dedicated entirely to US college students and new grads, connecting a marketplace of job-seeking students with employers who used its enterprise recruiting products to build employment brand and streamline campus hiring. Founded in 2009 by Andrew Maguire and Nathan Parcells and backed by 500 Global, LookSharp was acquired by WayUp in 2017; its internmatch.com domain now redirects to wayup.com and the brand no longer operates independently. This profile documents a defunct/acquired company with no public API or developer surface.

companies.name: OpenEnglish
companies.description: Open English is an online English-language learning company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Miami, serving primarily Latin American and Hispanic markets. It offers live, around-the-clock online classes with native-speaking teachers, self-paced interactive lessons, and mobile apps across consumer (B2C), business (Open English for Business), and children's (Open English Junior) programs. Backed by Insight Partners and other growth investors, it operates a consumer education platform and does not publish a public developer API program; its public GitHub organization holds internal open-source engineering forks rather than client SDKs.

companies.name: Pathgather
companies.description: Pathgather was an enterprise Learning Experience Platform (LXP), founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City, that helped large enterprises curate, share, and track learning content across their existing learning ecosystems. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Techstars, Pathgather (co-founded by CEO Eric Duffy) was one of the companies that established the LXP category before being acquired by Degreed in June 2018; all employees joined Degreed and the standalone product was wound down. Pathgather exposed a REST API in its operating years (a community Python client, tonybaloney/pathgather, remains on PyPI as historical evidence), but the company no longer operates independently: the pathgather.com domain is now parked and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record.

companies.name: Philon
companies.description: Philon is a Y Combinator-backed robotics research company building open-source, general-purpose humanoid robots capable of performing unsafe, repetitive, or boring tasks. Philon develops foundational AI models for embodied agents, including Holo 1.0, a generalist vision-language-action model that navigates virtual 3D worlds and completes hour-long objectives, alongside research on generative memory, focused attention for massive context windows, and latent steering of action experts. The company publishes its models and research code openly on GitHub.

companies.name: Planqc
companies.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

companies.name: uNow (UniversityNow)
companies.description: UniversityNow, Inc. (uNow) was a San Francisco-based higher-education startup founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) that built competency-based, self-paced online degree programs for working adults. It operated New Charter University, acquired Patten University in 2012, and its learning platform was sold to Penn Foster Education Group in 2016 and National University System in 2018. The company is defunct and unow.com now redirects to a dead page; it published no public API.

companies.name: CourseGuide
companies.description: CourseGuide is a portfolio-lead company in the API Evangelist network, surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and mapped to coursereport.com. Course Report is a consumer-facing education platform that helps prospective students discover, compare, and review coding bootcamps, certification courses, and professional training programs, aggregating 900+ programs and tens of thousands of alumni reviews alongside rankings, career-matching tools, and guidance content. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment; this profile remains a lead with only domain-security posture and public web properties captured.

companies.name: Elwyn
companies.description: Elwyn is a Pennsylvania-headquartered nonprofit human services organization founded in 1852, providing services to children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism, and behavioral health needs. Elwyn describes itself as "the longest-running human services nonprofit of its kind in the nation," operating across Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, and California with approximately 4,000 employees. The organization delivers six core service lines: Adult Behavioral Health Services, Children's Behavioral Health Services, Crisis Services, Early Learning Services, Educational Services, and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities Services. Elwyn is a service-delivery nonprofit, not a software or API provider. It publishes no public APIs, OpenAPI documents, SDKs, developer portal, or open-data feeds. Its digital presence is limited to its marketing site (elwyn.org), program pages, news, and donation/contact forms. This profile documents the organization's mission and the absence of any public API or developer surface.

companies.name: Frontrow
companies.description: FrontRow was an India-based edtech company that operated an online learning platform teaching extracurricular skills and hobbies — such as music, singing, guitar, drawing, chess and other creative pursuits — to learners through recorded video courses and community-driven classes. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of the last enrichment pass the product has shut down: its primary domain frontrow.co.in 301-redirects to a Medium shutdown announcement confirming "FrontRow shut down a few months ago," and no developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface exists. This entry is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: Generalist AI
companies.description: Generalist AI is a frontier AI research and product company founded in 2024 that is building general intelligence for the physical world. Rather than manufacturing robots, Generalist builds the embodied foundation models — the "brain" — that run across many robot types and hardware configurations, with an emphasis on dexterity and autonomy. Its founding team of researchers, roboticists, and operators comes from Google DeepMind, Boston Dynamics, and OpenAI, with prior work on PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics, Atlas, Spot, and the scaling of large language models. The company's GEN-1 model (April 2026) is described as the first general-purpose model to reach mastery of simple physical tasks, running with full autonomy. Generalist operates from the Bay Area (San Mateo / San Francisco) and Boston, and has raised more than $500M — including a $400M round at a roughly $2B valuation backed by Nvidia, Bezos Expeditions, Radical Ventures, 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, Hanabi Capital, and boldstart ventures. Generalist AI currently publishes no public API or developer program; this profile captures its company identity and web presence for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Maqsad
companies.description: Maqsad is Pakistan's leading online entry-test preparation platform, helping students prepare for standardized university entrance exams including MDCAT, ECAT, BCAT and O-Level. The platform delivers daily live classes, recorded video lectures, 15,000+ practice MCQs per exam, weekly mock tests, real-time doubt-solving and academic counseling through student-facing mobile apps and web access. Founded in 2021 and backed by Speedinvest, Maqsad reports 4M+ downloads and tens of thousands of enrolled students placed into universities such as NUST, IBA and DUHS. It operates as a business-to-consumer education company and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation or developer portal.

companies.name: MommaZoo
companies.description: MommaZoo was a mobile web application for parent-teacher and school-community communication, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Built as an HTML5 cross-platform app, it let parents and teachers centralize class posts, homework, sign-ups, reminders, documents, and multi-channel messaging across devices and languages. The company is defunct - public activity ends around 2013 and the mommazoo.com domain is now parked - and an enrichment pass found no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

companies.name: Odyssey Ai
companies.description: Odyssey is an AI research lab building general-purpose world models — causal, multimodal systems that understand and simulate physical environments, generating long-form interactive video simulations from text or image prompts rather than text. Its research includes Odyssey-2 (a flagship world model producing multi-minute interactive simulations), Starchild-1 (a real-time multimodal world model), Agora-1 (a multi-agent world simulator), and PROWL-1 (a reinforcement-learning framework for adversarial environment exploration). Odyssey positions world models as foundational AI for robotics, gaming, healthcare, education, and 3D visual asset generation, and raised a $310M Series B. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC. At the time of this profile Odyssey publishes research, writing, and interactive demos but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: OnlineTyari
companies.description: OnlineTyari is one of India's largest online exam-preparation platforms, built by Next Door Learning Solutions Private Limited (Jaipur, Rajasthan) and acquired by Embibe in February 2020. Through its website and Android/iOS apps it helps students and job aspirants prepare for competitive government examinations such as SSC CGL, IBPS PO/Clerk, RRB, Railways NTPC, and various State PSC exams, offering mock tests, question banks, current-affairs updates, e-books, and study material in Hindi and English produced with independent tutors, coaching institutes, and subject authors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass, OnlineTyari operates as a consumer-facing exam-prep product and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

companies.name: Parasma
companies.description: Parasma is a San Francisco based biological compute startup building algorithms and hardware that train living human brain cells (cortical neurons on a chip) to perform computation for AI workloads. Founded in 2026 by Sean Cole and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch), the company grew out of research that taught a clump of lab-grown human neurons to play Doom, coverage of which appeared in Nature, The Economist, Scientific American, The Guardian and elsewhere. Parasma currently operates as an early-stage research company with a marketing and news website; it does not yet publish a public API, SDK, developer portal, or other machine-readable developer surface. This profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead so any future developer platform can be captured when it ships.

companies.name: 51Talk Koala (koalareading.com)
companies.description: koalareading.com serves 51Talk考拉外教官网, the marketing landing page for 51Talk's "Koala" online English foreign-teacher tutoring product aimed at Chinese K-12 learners. The site is a single-page property (hero banner plus footer) operated by 大生在线（深圳）文化传媒科技有限公司 of Shenzhen under ICP filing 粤ICP备2023085692号, with lizhen01@51talk.com published as the technical support contact. The profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio lead under the name "koalareading" (考拉阅读 / Koala Reading, a Chinese K-12 reading-comprehension edtech); the domain as observed on 2026-07-19 serves the 51Talk Koala product instead, and the relationship between the two is not asserted here. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, CLI, or machine-readable discovery surface, so this profile carries only probed evidence.

companies.name: 61draw
companies.description: 61draw (广东省六一线上非学科培训学校有限公司, Guangdong Liuyi Online Non-Academic Training School Co., Ltd.) is a China-based online children's art and non-academic education platform delivering live-broadcast art lessons to children roughly aged five to nine. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and Matrix Partners China, which co-led its Series B round, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. The company runs a consumer web and mobile presence at 61draw.com; no public developer, API, or documentation surface has been found during enrichment.

companies.name: 9Slides
companies.description: 9Slides was a cloud-based presentation platform, founded by Ruchit Garg in 2011, that let users combine slide decks (PowerPoint, PDF, Keynote, Prezi, Excel) with synchronized video and deliver them through an HTML5 player viewable on desktop, tablet, and mobile. It operated on a freemium model, charging for premium features such as an ad-free player, password-protected presentations, and viewer analytics, and later pivoted toward learning and training. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by employee-engagement platform Limeade. The 9slides.com domain no longer serves the product and now resolves to a parked/redirect landing page; no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

companies.name: Achieve3000
companies.description: Achieve3000 is a supplemental digital literacy solution for grades 3-12 that uses adaptive technology to personalize reading instruction, delivering differentiated nonfiction texts matched to each student's Lexile reading level to build vocabulary and comprehension. Originally an independent education-technology company backed by Insight Partners, Achieve3000 was acquired by McGraw Hill and is now offered as "Achieve3000 Literacy" within McGraw Hill's PreK-12 portfolio. Students and educators access the platform through their district's approved single sign-on (SSO); the product publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and demand tracking.

companies.name: Aemon
companies.description: Aemon is an autonomous AI research-and-development engineer founded in 2025 by Ray Xu and Richard Zhou and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Given an engineering problem and a measurable objective, Aemon reads state-of-the-art research, then generates, tests, and evolves thousands of candidate approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions that can exceed what human experts find. The team demonstrated the approach by setting a new world record on the NP-hard circle-packing optimization problem for under $10 of compute, beating a prior Google DeepMind result. Aemon is an early-stage, demo-first enterprise product headquartered in San Francisco; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Almentor
companies.description: Almentor is a Dubai (UAE) based video e-learning platform delivering the largest high-quality Arabic continuous-learning video library, founded in 2016 and launched in January 2018 by Ihab Fikry and Ibrahim Kamel. It serves both individual learners (B2C) and organizations (B2B via business.almentor.net) with paid courses, free talks, crash courses, and books across health, humanities, technology, entrepreneurship, business management, lifestyle, and corporate communication, delivered by hundreds of experts and educators across the MENA region. Backed by Partech, Almentor has delivered more than three million learning experiences. Almentor publishes no public developer/API program; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: AltSchool
companies.description: AltSchool was an American education-technology company founded in 2013 by former Google executive Max Ventilla to build a network of small private "lab" schools around a personalized, student-directed learning model, using those campuses to develop a K-12 software platform for assignments and progress tracking. It raised more than $170 million from investors including Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mark Zuckerberg's CZI, and Peter Thiel. In 2017-2019 the company closed or handed off its for-profit schools (to Higher Ground Education) and pivoted to selling the software as "Altitude Learning," with Ventilla stepping down as CEO. The venture is now defunct as an independent operation: the altschool.com domain no longer resolves and altitudelearning.com redirects to Guidepost Montessori. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found; this record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio company profile.

companies.name: Blinkist
companies.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

companies.name: Blue Studios.io, BlueStudios
companies.description: Blue Studios (bluestudios.io), tagline "Where Families Flourish," is a family-focused technology company backed by 500 Global that builds consumer digital products and experiences for households. Its portfolio spans Wallio, a collaborative finance app for couples and families; Blue Studios Education, an edutainment streaming and learning platform; Blue Studios Entertainment, a family-oriented media production division; and Blueniverse, the ecosystem tying the products together. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation — this profile is a consumer-company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API producer.

companies.name: BlueLabs
companies.description: BlueLabs (withbluelabs.ai) is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building toward "emotional intelligence at scale." Its core technology, Blue-JST, is described as a novel dual reward mechanism designed to balance relationships and utility — an approach grounded in reward modeling and reinforcement learning. The company is backed by Forerunner Ventures and is actively hiring research talent. As of this profile it publishes a single marketing site (built on Webflow) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface; this record will be enriched as a developer- or agent-facing surface emerges.

companies.name: Bluelearn
companies.description: Bluelearn was an India-based community-driven learning and edtech startup backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive - its primary domain (bluelearn.in) no longer serves a product site and instead resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander page, with no reachable HTTPS endpoint, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. No OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found to search, generate, or derive from. This profile remains a lead pending any revived public developer surface.

companies.name: BrightBytes
companies.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Briko Robotics
companies.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

companies.name: Buildspace
companies.description: Buildspace was an online education platform and community that billed itself as "the biggest school in the world for people who wanted to work on their own ideas," running six-week cohort-based programs to help entrepreneurs and builders ship their own projects and startups. Backed by a16z, the company wound down its operations; its site now serves only a farewell letter and final video. It was a consumer education and community product, not an API provider, and exposes no public developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

companies.name: Byjus
companies.description: Byju's is an Indian educational technology company founded in 2011 by Byju Raveendran and Divya Gokulnath and headquartered in Bengaluru, India. It offered app-based adaptive learning for K-12 students and preparation for competitive exams such as JEE, NEET, and civil services, and expanded through acquisitions including Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Toppr, Osmo, Epic, and Great Learning. Once among the world's most valuable edtech startups, the company entered insolvency proceedings in India following a widely reported financial collapse. Byju's does not publish a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer surface.

companies.name: Chalkable
companies.description: Chalkable was a K-12 education technology company that provided a cloud-based student information system (SIS), learning management, and an education "app store" letting schools run third-party classroom apps on top of shared student data. Its developer platform exposed a RESTful API (OAuth 2.0) over school data points such as student and teacher scheduling, real-time attendance, grading and discipline records, announcements, messaging, and notifications, with partner apps rendered inside an iframe within the Chalkable classroom. Chalkable was acquired by PowerSchool on October 12, 2016, and the product line was absorbed into PowerSchool; the original developer surface (dev.chalkable.com and classroom.chalkable.com/Developer) is no longer operational. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

companies.name: changeducation
companies.description: ChangEducation is an integrated teaching-service provider of artificial-intelligence and STEAM curriculum systems, surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It builds AI and STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics) curriculum products and teaching services for the Chinese K-12 education market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing website (changeducation.cn, which redirects to a JavaScript-rendered landing page) with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile remains an identity-only lead with no technical API artifacts.

companies.name: Clutch Learning
companies.description: Clutch Learning (Clutch Prep) was a Miami-based education-technology startup founded in 2011 that helped more than two million college students learn through thousands of short-form, topic-based video tutorials and practice problems across subjects such as chemistry, physics, biology, accounting, and calculus. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), the company was acquired by Pearson in 2022 and folded into the Pearson+ study platform, where the offering now lives as Pearson Channels. The standalone clutchprep.com product is no longer independently operated. The domain 301-redirects to pearson.com/channels, and the company exposes no independent developer portal, public API, SDKs, or event surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

companies.name: Cultivate
companies.description: Cultivate was an AI-powered digital leadership and coaching platform that analyzed leaders' own opt-in digital communication data to deliver hyper-personalized, privacy-preserving coaching insights and recommendations for people managers. Founded through an Entrepreneur in Residence program at Samsung NEXT by Joseph Freed, Samir Meghani, and Andy Horng, and backed by Trinity Ventures, Silicon Valley Data Capital, and Bloomberg Beta, Cultivate was acquired by employee listening and people-analytics company Perceptyx on February 15, 2022, where it became the basis for Perceptyx's "Cultivate Intelligent Coaching" product. Cultivate operated as an enterprise HR/leadership SaaS and did not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the company no longer exists as an independent entity.

companies.name: Discovered Materials
companies.description: Discovered Materials (legally matforge inc) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) startup based in San Francisco building AI scientists for the semiconductor industry. The company uses swarms of AI agents to run the full materials-discovery pipeline - generating candidate materials, synthesizing them, and testing them in physical laboratories - to find novel materials for datacenters and fabrication facilities. Their stated goal is to compress a process that traditionally takes 10+ years of lab work into months, targeting 10x-better alternatives for applications such as nanoscale interconnects. Founded by Akash Ramdas (Stanford materials-science PhD/postdoc) and Advaith Sridhar (Carnegie Mellon AI, formerly Luma Labs and Persona AI). At the time of profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this entry is an enrichment lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: docin
companies.description: docin (豆丁网, docin.com) is a Chinese C2C document-sharing platform operated by Beijing Docin Century Network Technology (北京豆丁世纪网络技术有限公司) that faces the global market. The platform hosts over 1.3 billion documents, books, magazines, and publications spanning education, architecture and construction, business and contracts, medical and psychological materials, industry reports, and legal documents, supporting both learning and practical application. It offers a "豆丁书房" (Docin Reading Room) mobile reading app and VIP membership tiers. docin was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Probing found no public developer or API platform: open.docin.com 301-redirects to the homepage, /app/api returns 404, and no /.well-known discovery documents are published.

companies.name: Edia
companies.description: Edia is an AI platform for K-12 school districts focused on improving student outcomes. Its products span AI math tutoring (reported 8-23% score improvements), attendance intervention to reduce chronic absenteeism (up to 30% reduction), and District Intelligence analytics that consolidate data from student information systems (SIS), learning management systems (LMS), behavior, and wellness sources into a single view for educators and administrators. Edia reports serving 200+ districts and 500K+ students. The company is backed by Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. Edia does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specification, so this profile carries only verifiable company identity and probed domain-security posture.

companies.name: Edmodo
companies.description: Edmodo was an education technology company that operated a K-12 social learning network and learning management platform connecting teachers, students, and parents, and at its peak ran a developer platform and app store for third-party education apps. It was acquired by NetDragon in 2018 and the service was shut down in September 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the edmodo.com domain resolves only to a parked lander page and exposes no live developer, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: eduFire
companies.description: eduFire was an online education startup surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-19 found that the company's primary domain, edufire.com, no longer resolves (no DNS A or NS records), indicating the company is defunct. No live developer portal, API surface, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or any other artifact could be located to enrich, so this profile remains an identity-only stub.

companies.name: Edukart
companies.description: EduKart was an Indian online education startup, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), that sold certificate, diploma and degree courses from partner universities and training institutes to Indian learners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is now defunct — repeated probes of edukart.com find a parked hosting placeholder rather than a live business, and no developer, API, documentation or SDK surface exists to catalog.

companies.name: EduPristine
companies.description: EduPristine is a Mumbai-based finance, accounting, and analytics training institute founded in 2008, offering classroom and online certification-prep and professional up-skilling programs. Its catalog spans financial modeling, CFA, FRM, ACCA, US CPA and US CMA, business analytics and data science, digital marketing, financial accounting (Big 4 aligned), and healthcare/medical coding. EduPristine runs training centers across India alongside self-paced and instructor-led online courses, and is part of Adtalem Global Education. Sector: edtech. No public developer API or documented API surface was found during enrichment; the corporate website sits behind a WAF that blocks automated discovery of a well-known or developer surface.

companies.name: English Central
companies.description: English Central is an online English language learning platform that combines a large library of authentic video content with speech-recognition-driven pronunciation practice, adaptive vocabulary and quiz tools, and live one-on-one lessons with tutors. It serves individual learners as well as schools, universities, and enterprise/partner programs (including regional partners in Japan and elsewhere). Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the consumer education / EdTech sector. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; partner integrations appear to be handled privately.

companies.name: Enuma, Inc.
companies.description: Enuma, Inc. is a Berkeley, California educational technology company that builds award-winning, self-guided digital learning apps for young children, including the Todo Math series, Todo Classroom, and the Kitkit School / Enuma Global program. Founded by Sooinn Lee and Gunho Lee, Enuma designs research-based, game-like early literacy and numeracy experiences that work for all learners, including children with special needs and those in low-resource settings. The company co-won the $10M Global Learning XPRIZE for its open-source Kitkit School tablet curriculum. Enuma is a consumer and classroom education company that ships mobile applications through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Flourish
companies.description: Flourish (Flourish Labs) is a New York City based artificial intelligence research company building, in its own words, "human-level intelligence with human-level efficiency." Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the lab concentrates on advanced machine learning systems and foundational AI research rather than a public developer platform. At the time of profiling it publishes a marketing website but exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation, MCP server, or other developer surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio-lead stub and enriched with a live domain-security probe of its website host.

companies.name: Funderful
companies.description: Funderful was an alumni fundraising software platform for universities and higher-education advancement teams, founded in 2013 by Raimonds Kulbergs and headquartered in Riga, Latvia. It helped advancement offices run donation campaigns, track donors, and pioneer conversational chatbots to re-engage alumni, with clients including UC Berkeley, Georgetown, London Business School, and Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Funderful joined 500 Startups (Batch 20) and raised seed funding before being acquired by Ruffalo Noel Levitz (RNL) in February 2019. The company is defunct as an independent entity and its domain (funderful.com) no longer resolves; enrichment found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

companies.name: GamerzClass
companies.description: GamerzClass was a Copenhagen, Denmark-based online esports education platform, founded in 2018, that offered structured masterclasses and one-on-one coaching from professional players across titles such as Counter-Strike, League of Legends, and Dota 2. Backed by 500 Global, ByFounders, Bumble Ventures, and TrueSight Ventures, the company raised roughly USD 2.5M before being acquired by US-based esports coaching marketplace Metafy in May 2022. The gamerzclass.com domain no longer serves a live site and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Gartner
companies.description: Gartner is a global research and advisory firm providing information, advice, and tools to business leaders across IT, finance, HR, customer service, sales, marketing, supply chain, and legal functions. Gartner does not publish a public developer API; this repository tracks the company and any partner or technical artifacts that surface over time.

companies.name: GMR
companies.description: GMR (General Mining Research) is a crypto and Web3 company backed by Multicoin Capital and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its public presence is a single-page web application at gmr.xyz identifying it as "General Mining Research" with a general contact at info@gmr.xyz. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, well-known discovery surface, or SDK/CLI could be found — the only machine-verifiable signal is the domain's TLS/DNS security posture. This profile remains a lead awaiting a published API or developer surface to enrich further.

companies.name: InstaEDU
companies.description: InstaEDU was an online, on-demand tutoring platform founded in 2011 in San Francisco that connected students with tutors for live one-on-one help across a range of academic subjects. Backed by Battery Ventures and Social Capital, the company was acquired by Chegg in 2014 and folded into the Chegg Tutors service, which Chegg subsequently wound down in 2021. There is no independent InstaEDU developer program, public API, developer portal, or live domain today (instaedu.com no longer resolves) — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Izif
companies.description: Izif (إعزف) is an online music education platform for the Arabic-speaking world, positioning itself as the largest platform for teaching music in Arabic. It offers a subscription library of more than 2,000 instructional videos across roughly ten popular Arabic instruments — oud, guitar, violin, piano, ney, darbuka, qanun, vocals, and music theory — taught by elite Arab musicians, alongside music sheets and iOS/Android apps. A 500 Global portfolio company, Izif is a consumer EdTech subscription service and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

companies.name: Jumpcut
companies.description: Jumpcut (Jumpcut, Inc.) is a Y Combinator-backed, remote-first digital-media company founded in 2014 in Los Angeles that produces online courses about entrepreneurship and content creation — teaching viral YouTube growth, audience building, and launching digital products with marketing automation. It reached the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners. Jumpcut is a consumer education/creator business, not an API producer: it publishes no developer platform, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so there is no API surface to onboard here. As of this profile its primary domain jumpcut.com does not resolve (registered via Namecheap through 2032 but serving no DNS/website), and customers reported losing account access in late 2025, indicating the product has wound down. Retained as an identity-only network stub.

companies.name: juren
companies.description: Juren (巨人教育 / Juren Education) is a Chinese comprehensive basic-education training institution founded in 1994 and headquartered in Beijing (Zhongguancun, Haidian District). It is a B2C education and tutoring business — spanning brands such as Juren School, Juren 1-on-1, Xiao Juren, and Juren online school — offering courses in Chinese, English, mathematics, arts, study tours, and seasonal camps, plus education publishing and franchising. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found NO public developer, API, or technical-integration surface: the historic official domain juren.com does not resolve (DNS), juren.ai is a parked for-sale domain, and juren.cn is a Chinese-language marketing mirror with no developer section. This is a non-API B2C company lead retained for network completeness rather than API artifact enrichment.

companies.name: Kings
companies.description: Kings International Olympiads (kings.lt) is an international educational olympiads organization that runs academic competitions for students, operating a multi-language web platform served from kingsolympiad.com. It was surfaced through the 500 Global venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the organization publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery artifacts (/.well-known/*, llms.txt all resolve to the SPA shell, i.e. soft 404s).
